# ExpertCare: full text

> Services, guides, reference facts and area guides from https://expertcarerealestate.com/. Figures checked against official sources; each section lists its own.

## Questions people ask

**Can foreigners buy property in Dubai?**
Yes. Buyers of any nationality can own freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold areas, which include Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai and Palm Jumeirah, and they do not need a UAE residence visa to buy. [How to buy a home in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/how-to-buy-property-in-dubai/) takes you through each step.

**What fees do you pay when buying property in Dubai?**
On a ready home, about 7% of the price: the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT, a customary 2% agency fee plus VAT and the developer's NOC fee. [What it costs to buy](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai/) explains each one.

**Are off-plan payments protected in Dubai?**
Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 requires off-plan payments to go into an escrow account for the project, to be used only for its construction. Check the developer, the escrow account and the payment plan before you reserve; [buying off-plan in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-off-plan-in-dubai/) lists what to look for.

**Does buying property in Dubai give you a visa?**
Property worth AED 2 million or more lets an investor apply for a Golden Visa, which the Dubai Land Department and GDRFA describe as ten years and renewable. See [the Golden Visa through property](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/golden-visa-through-property/).

**Which areas of Dubai are freehold?**
Freehold areas were first designated in Regulation No. 3 of 2006 and more have been added since. They include every community in our [area guides](https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/), among them Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Palm Jumeirah, Jumeirah Village Circle, Arjan and Dubai Islands.


### Buying

**Can foreigners buy property in Dubai?**
Yes. Buyers of any nationality can own freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold areas, first set out in Regulation No. 3 of 2006 and extended since. They include Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Palm Jumeirah, Business Bay, Dubai Hills Estate, Jumeirah Village Circle and Dubai Creek Harbour. You do not need a UAE residence visa to buy. [How to buy a home in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/how-to-buy-property-in-dubai/) takes you through each step.

**How does ExpertCare work for a buyer?**
We take your brief, work out the full budget with the fees, shortlist homes whose adverts carry a valid Trakheesi permit, negotiate the offer and handle Form F, the developer's NOC and the transfer. The contract between you and us is Form B, the Dubai Land Department's standard buyer-broker agreement. [Buying property in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/buying-property-in-dubai/) sets out each step.

**What deposit do I pay when I agree to buy?**
By custom, 10% of the price when you sign Form F, RERA's standard sale contract between buyer and seller. It is market practice rather than a legal rule, and the deposit is held until the transfer.

**What is Form F?**
RERA's standard sale contract between buyer and seller, often called the MOU. It records the price, the deposit, who pays the developer's NOC fee and the transfer date. Form A is the seller's contract with their broker and Form B the buyer's; the [glossary](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-glossary/) defines each.

**Can I buy without visiting Dubai?**
Yes, through an attorney appointed with a power of attorney. One issued abroad must be notarised there, legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate, attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, translated into Arabic and issued no more than two years before it is used. [Buying property in Dubai from abroad](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-property-in-dubai-from-abroad/) covers identification, paying and borrowing.

**How do I know an advert is genuine?**
Every property advert in Dubai must show its Trakheesi permit number, and printed and video adverts carry a Madmoun QR code you can scan to confirm the advert is approved. Brokerages must also show their ORN and the broker's BRN. We check all three before a home goes on your shortlist.

**Should I buy ready or off-plan?**
A ready home is paid for at transfer and can be lived in or let from that day; an off-plan home is paid in stages while it is built. Both pay a 4% Dubai Land Department fee. [Off-plan or ready](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/off-plan-vs-ready-property-in-dubai/) compares them side by side.

### Off-plan

**Is my money protected when I buy off-plan?**
Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 requires off-plan payments to go into an escrow account for the project, used only for its construction and out of reach of the developer's creditors. Pay only into the escrow account named on the advert and in your agreement. [Buying off-plan in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-off-plan-in-dubai/) lists the checks.

**What is Oqood and what does it cost?**
The Dubai Land Department's interim register for off-plan sales. It records you as the buyer before a title deed exists, for 4% of the price plus AED 20. Developers may add their own administration charge, so ask for it in writing.

**What must an off-plan advert show?**
A Trakheesi permit for the unit itself, which every off-plan unit has needed since April 2024, the developer's name, the project's escrow account number and the expected completion date. Printed and video adverts also carry a Madmoun QR code.

**What does ExpertCare check before I reserve?**
The developer, the project's registration with the Dubai Land Department, the escrow account number, the project's status in the Dubai REST app, every instalment in the payment plan, the delay clause in the sale agreement and the service charge after handover. When you buy from a developer, the developer pays our commission. [Off-plan advisory](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/off-plan-advisory/) sets out the process.

**How long is the developer liable for defects?**
One year from handover for defective mechanical, electrical, sanitary and sewerage installations, and ten years from the completion certificate for structural defects, under Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019. Any agreement to the contrary is void. [Handover and snagging in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/handover-and-snagging-in-dubai/) explains what to inspect.

**What happens if I stop paying?**
After a 30-day notice served through DLD, the developer may terminate under Law No. 13 of 2008 as amended by Law No. 19 of 2020. It may keep up to 40% of the unit's value if the project is more than 60% complete, or up to 25% below that. It refunds the rest within a year, or within 60 days of reselling the unit, whichever is sooner.

**Can I sell an off-plan home before handover?**
Yes, subject to the developer's conditions for a resale NOC. Under Article 3 of Law No. 13 of 2008 every such sale must be entered in DLD's interim register or it is void.

### Selling

**How does ExpertCare sell a home?**
We value it against our analysis of the Dubai Land Department's open transaction data, sign Form A, obtain the Trakheesi permit, market the home, qualify buyers, run viewings, bring you every offer in writing, prepare Form F, obtain the developer's NOC and attend the transfer at the registration trustee. [Selling property in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/sell/) sets out the process.

**What is Form A?**
RERA's standard contract between a seller and the broker marketing the home. It records the asking price, the listing term and the commission, and it is signed before the home is advertised.

**Who pays the fees when I sell?**
By custom the buyer pays the 4% Dubai Land Department transfer fee, although DLD's own schedule divides it equally and the split can be agreed in Form F. The developer's NOC fee of AED 500 to 5,000 is split as agreed in Form F. Our commission is agreed in Form A.

**How is my home valued?**
Against recent sales of similar homes in the same building or community, using our analysis of DLD's open transaction data on the [prices pages](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-prices/), and the homes competing with yours. The statistics are our analysis, not a DLD valuation.

**Can I sell with a tenant in place?**
Yes. The tenancy and its Ejari contract pass to the buyer. If the buyer wants vacant possession, ending the tenancy at expiry because of the sale needs at least 12 months' notice served through a notary public or by registered mail.

**Can I sell with unpaid service charges?**
No. Under Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 unpaid service charges are a lien on the home and it cannot be sold until they are paid. [Service charges in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/service-charges-in-dubai/) explains how they are set and checked.

**Can I sell from abroad?**
Yes, through an attorney under a power of attorney that is notarised in the country of issue, legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate, attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, translated into Arabic and issued within two years. DLD's fully digital sale service needs an Emirates ID, a UAE Pass and a UAE bank account, so non-residents use the trustee office or an attorney.

### Renting

**Is Ejari registration mandatory?**
Yes. Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 requires every tenancy contract to be registered with RERA through Ejari. Online registration costs AED 177.75; at a registration trustee centre the fees are AED 100, AED 10 and AED 10 plus a AED 95 service fee and VAT. The landlord, the tenant or an attorney can register it.

**How is rent paid in Dubai?**
Rent is quoted per year and, by market practice, paid in advance by post-dated cheques from a UAE bank account. The number of cheques is agreed with the landlord and written into the contract, and fewer cheques can bring the rent down.

**How much can my rent go up at renewal?**
Only within Decree No. 43 of 2013. If the rent is up to 10% below the Smart Rental Index average for similar homes there is no increase; the limit is 5% if it is 11% to 20% below, 10% if 21% to 30% below, 15% if 31% to 40% below, and 20% if more than 40% below.

**How much notice must I get if the landlord will not renew?**
At least 90 days before the contract ends, unless the contract says otherwise. To take the home back to sell it or for the owner or a first-degree relative to move in, the landlord must give at least 12 months' notice through a notary public or by registered mail.

**When do I get my security deposit back?**
At the end of the tenancy, less any deductions agreed for damage beyond normal wear. A written condition report with photographs at move-in and move-out protects both sides.

**What does ExpertCare do for tenants?**
We shortlist homes that fit your brief, confirm each advert carries a Trakheesi permit, negotiate the rent, cheques and deposit, check the landlord's title deed, draw up the contract and register it on Ejari. [Renting a home in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/rent/) sets out the steps, and our fee is agreed in writing before you sign.

**Should I rent or buy when I move to Dubai?**
Most people rent first. A tenancy can be left with at least 90 days' notice at expiry, while a ready home carries about 7% in fees on top of the price. [Relocation to Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/relocation-to-dubai/) sets out both routes.

### Letting and management

**What does ExpertCare's property management include?**
Finding and vetting the tenant, the contract and Ejari registration, banking the cheques and paying you the rent, maintenance, inspections with written reports, renewal notices and rent proposals within the law, and an annual statement. The fee is a share of the annual rent, agreed in writing. [Property management in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/landlords/) has the detail.

**How much can I raise the rent?**
Only when the rent is more than 10% below the Smart Rental Index average for similar homes: by 5% if it is 11% to 20% below, 10% if 21% to 30% below, 15% if 31% to 40% below, and 20% if more than 40% below, under Decree No. 43 of 2013. [Renting out property in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/renting-out-property-in-dubai/) has the table.

**How much notice must I give a tenant?**
At least 90 days before the contract ends to change the terms or not renew, unless the contract says otherwise. To take the home back to sell it, or for you or a first-degree relative to live in, at least 12 months through a notary public or by registered mail.

**Do I pay tax on rental income?**
The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals, and under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023 a person's rental income from property in their own name is not subject to corporate tax when the activity does not require a licence. Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT. Your country of residence may tax the income.

**Who pays the service charges?**
Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 defines service charges as charges collected from owners. RERA must approve them, and you can check the approved figure for any building on DLD's Service Charge Index. Take them off the rent before judging the return.

**Can I let my home for short stays?**
With a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism, which individual owners can obtain for their own homes. Shared housing needs a separate permit under Law No. 4 of 2026. Check the current requirements and fees before you list.

**How does ExpertCare work out a return for investors?**
The likely annual rent from the Smart Rental Index and recent lets, less the approved service charge and the management fee, against the price plus the buying fees from the [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/). We show the inputs with their sources rather than a headline percentage, and we do not give investment advice. [Investor services](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/investor-services/) explains the method.

### Fees, visas and law

**What fees do I pay when buying a ready home?**
About 7% of the price. That covers the 4% Dubai Land Department transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees and the registration trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT (AED 2,000 plus VAT under AED 500,000). It also covers the customary 2% agency fee plus VAT and the developer's NOC fee of AED 500 to 5,000. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works it out for any price.

**Is the 2% agency fee set by law?**
No. 2% of the price plus VAT is the customary rate on a resale in Dubai, agreed with your broker in Form B. On an off-plan purchase from a developer, the developer pays the broker and the buyer pays nothing extra.

**How much property do I need for a Golden Visa?**
Property worth AED 2 million or more, in one property or several. The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA describe the visa as ten years and renewable; the federal portal shows a different term, so confirm it when you apply. Joint owners need a share worth AED 2 million. [The Golden Visa through property](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/golden-visa-through-property/) has the published rules.

**Can I get a residence visa with property under AED 2 million?**
The Dubai Land Department lists a two-year investor residence visa: a sole owner qualifies with property of any value, and a joint owner needs a share of at least AED 400,000. In April 2026 GDRFA Dubai and DLD agreed to move property residency services into GDRFA Dubai's system, so confirm the channel and fees before you apply.

**Is there tax on property in Dubai?**
The UAE has no personal income tax. Rental income from property held in a person's own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is required, under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023. Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT, and the first supply of a new residential property within three years of completion is zero-rated. [Dubai property facts](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-facts/) lists every rule with its source.

**Which laws protect buyers and tenants?**
Law No. 7 of 2006 on property registration and freehold ownership, Law No. 8 of 2007 on off-plan escrow accounts, Law No. 13 of 2008 on the interim register, Law No. 26 of 2007 and Law No. 33 of 2008 on landlords and tenants, Decree No. 43 of 2013 on rent increases and Law No. 6 of 2019 on jointly owned property and developer liability. Each is cited on [Dubai property facts](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-facts/).

## Buying a home in Dubai with ExpertCare

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/buying-property-in-dubai/

A buyer's broker for resale and off-plan homes: the shortlist, every advert checked, the price negotiated, one adviser to the title deed.

### In short

- ExpertCare acts for buyers of ready and off-plan homes in Dubai's freehold areas, whether you live in the UAE or abroad.
- On a resale the customary agency fee is 2% of the price plus VAT, paid by the buyer. On an off-plan purchase from a developer, the developer pays the broker and you pay nothing extra for our work.
- Before the first viewing you see the whole number: the price plus the Dubai Land Department, trustee and agency fees.

### How it works

1. **Brief and budget.** We take your brief: areas, type, size, move-in date and how you will pay. Then we work out the full budget with the [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/), every DLD, trustee and agency fee included.
2. **Form B.** Form B is RERA's standard contract between a buyer and a broker. It records what we do for you and our commission before any viewing takes place.
3. **Shortlist and viewings.** We shortlist homes that fit the brief, check each advert's Trakheesi permit, look up the building's approved service charges and arrange the viewings.
4. **Offer and Form F.** We negotiate the price and the terms and prepare Form F, the sale contract between you and the seller. By custom you pay a 10% deposit when it is signed, held until the transfer.
5. **NOC and transfer.** We obtain the developer's no-objection certificate, book the registration trustee and attend the transfer with you or your attorney.
6. **Title deed, and after.** The title deed is issued in your name. The same adviser stays on for the move, the Ejari if you let, and snagging if the home is new.

### What we check before you offer

- The advert carries a valid Trakheesi permit number and, on printed and video adverts, a Madmoun QR code we scan
- The building's service charges approved by RERA, looked up on DLD's Service Charge Index, and whether any are unpaid, because a home cannot be sold while they are
- Recent sale prices for the same building or community, from our analysis of DLD's open transaction data on the [prices pages](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-prices/)

### What buying costs

On a ready home, plan for about 7% on top of the price. That covers the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees and the trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT (AED 2,000 plus VAT under AED 500,000). It also covers the customary 2% agency fee plus VAT and the developer's NOC fee of AED 500 to 5,000.

By custom the buyer pays the whole 4% transfer fee, although a different split can be agreed in Form F.

Calculator: https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/

### If you buy off-plan

When you buy from a developer before the building is complete, the developer pays our commission and you pay nothing extra. You pay in stages into the project's escrow account, which under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 can be used only to build that project, and the purchase is registered on Oqood for 4% of the price plus AED 20.

Our [off-plan advisory](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/off-plan-advisory/) covers the developer and project checks, the payment plan and the handover.

### If you live outside the UAE

You do not need a residence visa to buy. A valid passport identifies you at the registration trustee, and if you cannot attend, an attorney signs for you. A power of attorney issued abroad must be notarised, legalised, attested, translated into Arabic and issued within two years.

[Buying property in Dubai from abroad](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-property-in-dubai-from-abroad/) covers identification, paying and visas.

### What it costs

On a resale the customary agency fee is 2% of the price plus VAT, paid by the buyer and agreed in Form B; on an off-plan purchase from a developer, the developer pays us and you pay nothing extra.

### Questions

**Do buyers pay an agency fee in Dubai?**
On a resale, yes. The customary fee is 2% of the price plus VAT, paid by the buyer and agreed in Form B, the contract between you and your broker.

**Is a buyer's broker free when buying off-plan?**
When you buy from a developer, the developer pays the broker's commission and you pay nothing extra for the broker's work. You still pay the 4% Oqood registration fee plus AED 20 to the Dubai Land Department.

**How much should I budget on top of the price?**
About 7% for a ready home. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) itemises every fee for any price.

**Can I buy without living in the UAE?**
Yes. Buyers of any nationality can own freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold areas, and a valid passport identifies a non-resident at the registration trustee.

**What is Form B?**
RERA's standard contract between a buyer and the broker acting for them. It sets out what the broker does and the commission, before any viewing.

**What deposit do I pay when I agree to buy?**
By custom, 10% of the price when you sign Form F, the sale contract with the seller. It is market practice rather than a legal rule, and it is held until the transfer.

## Selling your Dubai property with ExpertCare

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/sell/

A valuation from real sales data, a permitted listing, qualified buyers and a transfer handled from the first viewing to the trustee office.

### In short

- ExpertCare values your home against recent sales in the same building or community, markets it under a Trakheesi permit, and handles offers, Form F, the developer's NOC and the transfer.
- The process runs from Form A, the listing agreement, to the registration trustee office where the buyer pays and the title deed changes hands.
- By custom the buyer pays the 4% DLD transfer fee. Our commission is agreed in Form A before marketing begins.

### How it works

1. **Valuation.** We price the home from our analysis of DLD's open transaction data for the building or community and the homes competing with yours. You get a written range and the reasons behind it.
2. **Form A.** Form A is RERA's standard contract between a seller and the broker marketing the home. It records the asking price, the term and our commission.
3. **Trakheesi permit.** Every property advert in Dubai must show a Trakheesi permit number, so we apply for the permit before the listing goes live. Printed and video adverts also carry a Madmoun QR code.
4. **Marketing.** Photography, a listing on the portals and a direct approach to buyers already briefed with us. Every advert shows our ORN and the adviser's BRN.
5. **Viewings and offers.** We qualify each buyer, run the viewings and bring you every offer in writing.
6. **Form F.** Once you accept an offer we prepare Form F, the sale contract. By custom the buyer pays a 10% deposit on signing, held until the transfer, and the contract fixes the transfer date.
7. **NOC and transfer.** We obtain the developer's no-objection certificate, confirm nothing is owed on service charges, book the registration trustee and attend the transfer. You are paid at the trustee office.

### How we value your home

A valuation starts with what similar homes in the same building or community have sold for, using our analysis of the Dubai Land Department's open transaction data on the [prices pages](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-prices/), and the homes on the market now.

- Floor, view and orientation, which separate two homes of the same size in the same tower
- Whether the home is vacant or let, and the rent and term if it is let

The price statistics are our analysis of an open dataset, not a DLD valuation.

### The documents a sale needs

- Your title deed, and your passport or Emirates ID
- Form A, signed before the home is marketed
- The Trakheesi advertising permit for the listing
- The developer's no-objection certificate, for a fee of AED 500 to 5,000 that the developer sets; who pays it is agreed in Form F
- Confirmation that service charges are paid, because under Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 a home cannot be sold while they are unpaid

### The transfer day

Buyer and seller, or their attorneys, meet at a Dubai Land Department registration trustee office. By market practice the buyer pays the price by manager's cheque from a UAE bank. The 4% transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees and the trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT (AED 2,000 plus VAT under AED 500,000) are settled, the sale is registered and the title deed is issued in the buyer's name.

If the home is let, the tenancy passes to the buyer with its Ejari contract. Ending a tenancy at expiry because you are selling needs at least 12 months' notice served through a notary public or by registered mail.

### If you live outside the UAE

You can sell through an attorney. A power of attorney issued abroad must be notarised, legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate, attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, translated into Arabic and issued within two years, and its wording must clearly authorise the sale.

### What it costs

Our commission is agreed in Form A before marketing begins; by custom the buyer pays the 4% DLD transfer fee, and the developer's NOC fee of AED 500 to 5,000 is split as agreed in Form F.

### Questions

**What is Form A?**
RERA's standard contract between a seller and the broker marketing the home. It records the asking price, the listing term and the commission, and it is signed before the home is advertised.

**Who pays the DLD transfer fee when selling?**
By custom the buyer pays the full 4%. DLD's own schedule divides the fee equally between buyer and seller, so the two sides can agree a different split in Form F.

**Can I sell a home with a tenant in place?**
Yes. The tenancy and its Ejari contract pass to the buyer. If the buyer wants the home empty, ending the tenancy at expiry because of the sale needs at least 12 months' notice served through a notary public or by registered mail.

**Can I sell with unpaid service charges?**
No. Under Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 unpaid service charges are a lien on the home, and it cannot be sold until they are paid.

**How long does a sale take?**
Form F fixes the transfer date, so the timing depends on the buyer's funding and the developer's NOC.

## Renting a home in Dubai with ExpertCare

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/rent/

A tenant's adviser who shortlists, checks the landlord, negotiates the terms and registers the contract on Ejari.

### In short

- ExpertCare finds rental homes for tenants across Dubai, negotiates the rent and the number of cheques, checks the landlord's title deed and registers the tenancy on Ejari.
- Every tenancy contract must be registered with RERA through Ejari; online registration costs AED 177.75.
- At renewal the rent can rise only within the bands of Decree No. 43 of 2013, and either side must give at least 90 days' notice to change the terms or not renew.

### How it works

1. **Brief.** Areas, type, size, furnished or not, pets, parking, budget and move-in date. If you are new to Dubai, tell us where you will work and where children will go to school, and we shortlist by commute.
2. **Shortlist and viewings.** We shortlist homes that fit, confirm each advert carries a Trakheesi permit number, and arrange viewings in person or by video if you are still abroad.
3. **Offer and terms.** We negotiate the annual rent, the number of cheques, the security deposit, what is included and who handles maintenance, and put the agreed terms in writing before any contract is drawn up.
4. **Checks on the landlord.** We match the title deed to the person letting the home, or to their attorney under a power of attorney, so you pay the right person.
5. **Contract and payment.** The tenancy contract records the rent, the term, the deposit and the cheque dates. By market practice rent is paid in advance by post-dated cheques from a UAE bank account.
6. **Ejari.** The contract is registered with RERA through Ejari. Online registration costs AED 177.75. The landlord, the tenant or an attorney can register it.
7. **Move-in.** With the Ejari certificate in hand you open your DEWA account for electricity and water, collect the keys and record the condition of the home in writing, with photographs, so the deposit comes back cleanly.

### Rent, cheques and the deposit

Rent in Dubai is quoted per year and, by market practice, paid in advance by post-dated cheques from a UAE bank account. The number of cheques is agreed with the landlord, and fewer cheques often buys a lower rent.

The landlord holds a security deposit for the term and returns it at the end, less any deductions agreed for damage beyond normal wear.

### Why Ejari matters

Article 4 of Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007, as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008, requires every lease to be registered with RERA through Ejari. The certificate is what utilities, schools and government services ask for as proof of your address.

| Where you register | Fee |
| --- | --- |
| Dubai REST app or DLD website | AED 177.75 |
| Registration trustee centre | AED 100 + AED 10 + AED 10, plus a AED 95 service fee and VAT |

### Your rights at renewal

- **Rent increases.** The rent can rise at renewal only when it is more than 10% below the Smart Rental Index average for similar homes (Decree No. 43 of 2013). The rise is 5% if it is 11% to 20% below, 10% if 21% to 30% below, 15% if 31% to 40% below, and at most 20% if more than 40% below
- **Notice.** Either side must give at least 90 days' notice before the contract ends to change its terms or not renew, unless the contract says otherwise
- **Eviction at expiry.** A landlord who wants the home back to sell it, or for themselves or a first-degree relative to live in, must give at least 12 months' notice through a notary public or by registered mail

We check any proposed increase against the index before you sign the renewal.

### After you move in

Your adviser stays your contact for the term: maintenance the contract puts on the landlord, the renewal and the next move. If you later buy, the same adviser carries your brief across to [buying a home in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/buying-property-in-dubai/).

### What it costs

Our fee for finding and securing a rental home is agreed with you in writing before you sign the tenancy contract; Ejari registration costs AED 177.75 online.

### Questions

**Is Ejari registration mandatory for tenants in Dubai?**
Yes. Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 requires every tenancy contract to be registered with RERA through Ejari. Online registration costs AED 177.75, and the landlord, the tenant or an attorney can do it.

**How many cheques do I pay rent with?**
The number is agreed with the landlord and written into the contract. By market practice rent is paid in advance by post-dated cheques from a UAE bank account.

**Can my landlord raise the rent at renewal?**
Only within Decree No. 43 of 2013. If the rent is up to 10% below the index average for similar homes there is no increase; above that the limit is 5%, 10%, 15% or at most 20%, depending on how far below the average the rent sits.

**How much notice do I get if the landlord will not renew?**
At least 90 days before the contract ends, unless the contract says otherwise. To take the home back to sell it or move in, the landlord must give at least 12 months' notice through a notary public or by registered mail.

**When do I get my deposit back?**
At the end of the tenancy, less any deductions agreed for damage beyond normal wear. A written condition report with photographs at move-in and move-out is the best protection for both sides.

**Can I rent before my residence visa is issued?**
The tenancy is registered on Ejari with your identification, and each landlord decides what they accept. Tell us where you are in the visa process and we match the landlord and the timing to it.

---

## Letting and managing your Dubai property

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/landlords/

Tenants found and vetted, rent collected, maintenance handled and renewals kept within the law, with one statement a year.

### In short

- ExpertCare lets and manages homes for owners in Dubai: finding and vetting tenants, Ejari registration, rent collection, maintenance, renewals within the bands of Decree No. 43 of 2013, inspections and an annual statement.
- Our fee is a share of the annual rent, agreed in writing before we market the home.
- Rental income from property held in your own name is not subject to UAE corporate tax when the activity does not need a licence, under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023.

### How it works

1. **Onboarding.** We take the title deed, your identification, the keys and an inventory, confirm the service charges are paid and agree the asking rent against the Smart Rental Index and recent lets in the building.
2. **Marketing.** The listing goes live under a Trakheesi permit, with our ORN and the adviser's BRN on every advert on the portals.
3. **Tenant vetting.** We check each applicant's identification, employment and funds, and bring you a recommendation with the proposed rent, cheques and deposit.
4. **Contract and Ejari.** We draw up the tenancy contract, collect the cheques and the deposit, and register the contract with RERA through Ejari. Online registration costs AED 177.75.
5. **Rent and maintenance.** Cheques are banked on their dates and the rent is paid to you. Maintenance requests come to us, are priced, approved by you above an agreed limit and carried out.
6. **Inspections and renewals.** The home is inspected during the term with a written report. Before expiry we give any notice the law requires and propose the renewal rent within the Decree No. 43 of 2013 bands.
7. **Annual statement.** Once a year you receive a statement of rent received, our fee, maintenance and service charges, ready for your records or your accountant.

### How far the rent can rise at renewal

Decree No. 43 of 2013 ties any increase to how far the current rent sits below the Smart Rental Index average for similar homes:

| Current rent against the index average | Largest increase allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 10% below | No increase |
| 11% to 20% below | 5% |
| 21% to 30% below | 10% |
| 31% to 40% below | 15% |
| More than 40% below | 20% |

Changing the terms or not renewing needs at least 90 days' notice before the contract ends, unless the contract says otherwise. Taking the home back at expiry to sell it, or for you or a first-degree relative to live in, needs at least 12 months' notice through a notary public or by registered mail. We serve both on your instruction.

### Short-term lets and shared housing

A home let for short stays needs a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism, and individual owners can register their own homes. Law No. 4 of 2026 requires a separate permit before any unit is used as shared housing.

### What stays with the owner

- Service charges, which Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 defines as charges collected from owners; RERA must approve them, and you can check the approved figure on DLD's Service Charge Index
- Unpaid service charges are a lien on the home, and after a RERA-approved notice the owner has 30 days to pay before the claim is enforced
- Repairs the tenancy contract leaves with the landlord, approved by you above an agreed limit

### Tax on rental income

- The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals
- Under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, a person's income from property held in their own name is not subject to corporate tax, whatever the amount, as long as the activity is not carried out, and is not required to be carried out, under a licence
- Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT; commercial property is charged at 5%

> Your country of residence may tax income from Dubai property. ExpertCare does not give tax advice; check with an adviser there.

### What it costs

Our management fee is a share of the annual rent, agreed in writing before we market the home.

### Questions

**What does property management include?**
Finding and vetting the tenant, the contract and Ejari registration, banking the cheques and paying you the rent, maintenance, inspections with written reports, renewal notices and rent proposals within the law, and an annual statement.

**How much can I raise the rent at renewal?**
Only when the rent is more than 10% below the Smart Rental Index average for similar homes: by 5% if it is 11% to 20% below, 10% if 21% to 30% below, 15% if 31% to 40% below, and 20% if more than 40% below, under Decree No. 43 of 2013.

**How much notice must I give a tenant?**
At least 90 days before the contract ends to change the terms or not renew, unless the contract says otherwise. To take the home back to sell or move in, at least 12 months through a notary public or by registered mail.

**Do I pay tax on rent in Dubai?**
The UAE has no personal income tax, and under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023 a person's rental income from property in their own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is required. Your home country may tax it.

**Who pays the service charges, me or the tenant?**
Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 defines service charges as charges collected from owners. Budget for them each year and take them off the rent before judging the return.

**Can I let my home for short stays?**
With a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism, which individual owners can obtain for their own homes. Check its current requirements and fees before you list.

## Buying off-plan in Dubai with ExpertCare

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/off-plan-advisory/

The developer, the escrow account and the payment plan checked before you reserve, and the handover and snagging handled after.

### In short

- ExpertCare checks the developer, the project's Dubai Land Department registration, its escrow account and its payment plan before you reserve, and stays with you through Oqood registration, construction, handover and snagging.
- Under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 your payments go into the project's escrow account and can be used only to build that project.
- When you buy from a developer, the developer pays our commission and you pay nothing extra.

### How it works

1. **Brief.** Budget, areas, size, when you need the home and whether you will live in it or let it. We also ask how you will pay the instalments.
2. **Developer and project checks.** We confirm the developer, the project's registration with the Dubai Land Department, the escrow account number and its status in the Dubai REST app.
3. **Payment plan review.** We read every instalment: the amount, whether a date or a construction stage triggers it, what falls due at handover and what the sale agreement says about delays.
4. **Reservation and sale agreement.** You reserve, then sign the developer's sale and purchase agreement. We check it against the advert, the brochure and the payment plan before you sign.
5. **Oqood registration.** The purchase is registered on the Dubai Land Department's Oqood system for 4% of the price plus AED 20. Developers may add an administration charge; we get it in writing first.
6. **Construction to handover.** We track progress, flag each instalment before it falls due and arrange the handover appointment once the completion certificate is issued.
7. **Snagging and title deed.** We walk the home with you or an inspector, list defects for the developer in writing, and follow the Oqood registration through to your title deed.

### What we check before you reserve

- The developer's identity and the project's registration with the Dubai Land Department
- The escrow account number on the advert matches the one in your agreement; you pay into that account and no other
- The advert carries a Trakheesi permit for the unit, the developer's name, the escrow account number and the expected completion date
- The payment plan, the handover payment and the delay clause in the sale and purchase agreement
- The service charge you will pay once the building is handed over

### Where your money goes

Under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 off-plan buyers' payments go into an escrow account opened for that one project with an approved escrow agent. The money can be used only to build that project, and the developer's creditors cannot seize it.

If a buyer stops paying, Law No. 13 of 2008 as amended by Law No. 19 of 2020 lets the developer, after a 30-day notice served through DLD, keep up to 40% of the unit's value on a project more than 60% complete, or up to 25% below that.

### Handover and what the developer must fix

Once the project has its completion certificate, the developer must register sold units in the names of buyers who have met their obligations, under Article 8 of Law No. 13 of 2008. That is when your Oqood registration becomes a title deed.

| Defect | Developer liable for | Counted from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defective mechanical, electrical, sanitary and sewerage installations | 1 year | Handover |
| Defects in the structural parts of the building | 10 years | The completion certificate |

Both come from Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019, which makes any agreement to the contrary void.

### Selling before handover, and the Golden Visa

An off-plan home can be resold before completion, subject to the developer's conditions for a resale NOC. Under Article 3 of Law No. 13 of 2008 every such sale must be entered in DLD's interim register or it is void.

The Dubai Land Department's and GDRFA's pages on the property Golden Visa do not say whether an off-plan home counts towards the AED 2 million threshold. Confirm with GDRFA before you reserve with the visa in mind; our [Golden Visa service](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/golden-visa-through-property/) sets out the published rules.

### What it costs

On a purchase from the developer, the developer pays our commission and you pay nothing extra; on an off-plan resale from another buyer, the customary 2% plus VAT applies and is agreed in Form B.

### Questions

**Is my money protected when I buy off-plan in Dubai?**
Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 requires off-plan payments to go into an escrow account for the project, used only for its construction and out of reach of the developer's creditors.

**What does off-plan advice cost me?**
Nothing extra when you buy from the developer, because the developer pays the broker's commission. You still pay the 4% Oqood registration fee plus AED 20 to the Dubai Land Department.

**What should an off-plan advert show?**
A Trakheesi permit for the unit, the developer's name, the project's escrow account number and the expected completion date. Printed and video adverts also carry a Madmoun QR code.

**What happens if I cannot keep up the payments?**
After a 30-day notice served through DLD, the developer may terminate and keep up to 40% of the unit's value if the project is more than 60% complete, or up to 25% below that, and must refund the rest.

**When do I get the title deed?**
After the project receives its completion certificate, when the developer must register sold units in the names of buyers who have met their obligations under Article 8 of Law No. 13 of 2008.

## The Golden Visa through property, with ExpertCare

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/golden-visa-through-property/

What qualifies, where the official sources disagree, and how we prepare the purchase and the paperwork around it.

### In short

- Property worth AED 2 million or more, in one property or several, lets an investor in Dubai apply for a Golden Visa, which the Dubai Land Department and GDRFA describe as ten years and renewable.
- ExpertCare helps you choose and buy property that meets the threshold, assembles the document pack and books the appointment with the authority.
- Where the official sources disagree, on the visa term and on off-plan homes, we say so rather than pick a side. ExpertCare does not give immigration advice.

### How it works

1. **Eligibility check.** We look at what you own or plan to buy against the AED 2 million threshold, including how a joint owner affects it.
2. **Buying with the visa in mind.** If you are still buying, we shortlist ready homes that meet the threshold, since the official pages do not address off-plan homes, and run the purchase through to the title deed.
3. **Document pack.** Title deed, passport and photographs, assembled and checked against the authority's current list.
4. **Appointment.** We book the appointment with the Dubai Land Department or GDRFA Dubai, whichever runs the service when you apply, and go through the remaining steps the authority sets.

### The published rules

- Minimum value: property worth AED 2 million or more, in one property or several
- Jointly owned property counts only when the applicant's own share is worth AED 2 million or more
- The Dubai Land Department lists the Golden Visa fees for the main applicant as AED 9,884.75

### Where the sources disagree or are silent

The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai describe the visa as ten years and renewable. The federal government portal shows a different term for property investors. Confirm the term when you apply.

Neither the Dubai Land Department's page nor GDRFA's addresses off-plan homes. If the visa is part of your plan, confirm with GDRFA before relying on an off-plan purchase, or buy a ready home.

### Below AED 2 million

For property below the threshold, the Dubai Land Department's service page lists a two-year investor residence visa. A sole owner qualifies with a property of any value; a joint owner needs a share worth at least AED 400,000. DLD lists the investor fee as AED 10,212.50.

### Where to apply

The Dubai Land Department has run the Golden Visa and investor visa services for property owners. In April 2026 GDRFA Dubai and DLD agreed to move property residency services into GDRFA Dubai's system, so we check the current channel, requirements and fees at the time you apply.

> ExpertCare does not give immigration advice. Decisions on visas rest with the UAE authorities.

### What it costs

Our help with the purchase, the document pack and the appointment is part of buying with us; the Dubai Land Department lists the Golden Visa fee for the main applicant as AED 9,884.75, and the authority's fees apply when you apply.

### Questions

**How much property do I need for a Golden Visa in Dubai?**
Property worth AED 2 million or more, in one property or several, according to the Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai.

**Can joint owners combine their shares?**
GDRFA counts a jointly owned property only when the applicant's own share is worth AED 2 million or more.

**Does an off-plan property qualify?**
The official DLD and GDRFA pages do not say. Confirm with GDRFA before you buy with the visa in mind, or choose a ready home.

**How long is the Golden Visa?**
The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA describe it as ten years, renewable. The federal government portal shows a different term, so confirm it when you apply.

**Can I get a residence visa with property under AED 2 million?**
The Dubai Land Department lists a two-year investor residence visa: a sole owner qualifies with property of any value, and a joint owner needs a share of at least AED 400,000. DLD lists the fee as AED 10,212.50.

## Investing in Dubai property with ExpertCare

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/investor-services/

Homes sourced from the data, returns worked out the same way every time, and the letting handled by the team that found the home.

### In short

- ExpertCare sources property for investors in Dubai, works out the net return from the likely rent, the service charges and the buying fees, handles the purchase and then lets and manages the home.
- Our price statistics are our analysis of the Dubai Land Department's open transaction data, published on the [prices pages](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-prices/).
- We do not promise a yield and we do not give investment advice; we show the inputs with their sources so you can judge them.

### How it works

1. **Brief.** Budget, ready or off-plan, areas, whether you will let long-term or for short stays, and how long you plan to hold.
2. **The data.** We show recent sale prices and price per square foot for each area and building from our analysis of DLD's open data, and the rent the Smart Rental Index and recent lets suggest.
3. **Shortlist with the return worked out.** Each home comes with the same calculation: likely annual rent, less the approved service charge and the management fee, against the price plus the buying fees.
4. **Checks.** The advert's Trakheesi permit, the title deed, the building's approved service charges and whether any are unpaid, and on off-plan the escrow account and the developer.
5. **Purchase.** Form B, the offer, Form F, the developer's NOC and the transfer, or the reservation, sale agreement and Oqood registration on an off-plan home.
6. **Letting and management.** The same team markets the home, vets the tenant, registers the Ejari and manages the tenancy, with an annual statement of rent, fees and costs.

### How we work out a return

1. **The rent.** What similar homes in the building or community let for, from the Smart Rental Index and recent lets.
2. **The running costs.** The service charge RERA has approved for the building, looked up on DLD's Service Charge Index, plus our management fee and a provision for maintenance.
3. **The full price.** The price plus the buying fees: about 7% on a ready home, or 4% plus AED 20 on Oqood for an off-plan home, worked out with the [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/).

Net rent against the full price is the figure we compare homes on. We show the inputs rather than a headline percentage, because rent and service charges move.

### The data we use

We compute sales counts, median prices and median price per square foot by area and quarter from the Dubai Land Department's open transactions dataset. It is our analysis, not DLD's, published on the [prices pages](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-prices/) with the dataset and licence named.

Dubai recorded more than 270,000 real estate transactions worth AED 917 billion in 2025, 20% more than in 2024, according to the Dubai Media Office. Past figures do not tell you what a home will be worth.

### Letting after you buy

- Every tenancy is registered with RERA through Ejari, for AED 177.75 online
- At renewal the rent can rise only within the bands of Decree No. 43 of 2013, from nothing to at most 20%
- Short stays need a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism; shared housing needs a permit under Law No. 4 of 2026
- Our [property management](https://expertcarerealestate.com/landlords/) fee is a share of the annual rent, agreed in writing

### Tax, and buying from abroad

The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals. Under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, as explained by the Federal Tax Authority, a person's income from property held in their own name is not subject to corporate tax when the activity is not carried out, and is not required to be carried out, under a licence.

Non-residents buy with a passport. Your country of residence may tax your Dubai income; we do not give tax advice.

### What it costs

Buying through us costs the customary 2% plus VAT on a resale and nothing extra on an off-plan purchase from a developer; management is a share of the annual rent, agreed in writing.

### Questions

**What return can I expect on Dubai property?**
We do not promise a return. For each home we show the likely rent, the approved service charge, the management fee and the full price with fees, with sources, so you can judge the net figure.

**Where do your price figures come from?**
From our analysis of the Dubai Land Department's open real estate transactions dataset, published on our [prices pages](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-prices/). They are our statistics, not DLD valuations.

**Do I pay tax on rental income in Dubai?**
The UAE has no personal income tax, and under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023 rental income from property in your own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is required. Your home country may tax it.

**Can I let my investment for short stays?**
With a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism, which individual owners can obtain for their own homes. Check its current requirements before you buy with short stays in mind.

**Is off-plan or ready better for investors?**
Neither as a rule. A ready home can be let from the day of transfer; an off-plan home is paid in stages and earns nothing until handover. [Off-plan or ready](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/off-plan-vs-ready-property-in-dubai/) sets the two side by side.

**Can I invest without living in the UAE?**
Yes. Non-residents can own freehold property in Dubai's designated areas and buy with a passport.

## Moving to Dubai with ExpertCare

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/relocation-to-dubai/

Rent first or buy, which areas fit your commute, what a non-resident needs, and a home ready on the day you land.

### In short

- ExpertCare helps families and companies moving to Dubai find a home before they arrive: rent or buy, areas chosen by commute, viewings by video, Ejari and utilities handled.
- Most people rent first, because a tenancy can be in place within weeks and a purchase carries about 7% in fees on a ready home.
- You do not need a residence visa to buy, and a valid passport identifies a non-resident at the registration trustee.

### How it works

1. **Brief.** Who is moving, where you will work, where children will go to school, your budget, your arrival date and whether you want to rent or buy.
2. **Rent or buy.** We set out both routes with their costs and timing, so the choice is made on numbers.
3. **Areas by commute.** We map the shortlist against your workplace and schools using each area's Metro, tram and road links.
4. **Viewings.** In person if you are visiting, or by video with the adviser walking the home, with the advert's permit and the service charge checked first.
5. **Contract and Ejari.** For a rental we negotiate the rent, cheques and deposit, check the landlord's title deed, draw up the contract and register it on Ejari for AED 177.75 online.

### Renting first or buying

|  | Renting | Buying |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upfront | Rent in advance by post-dated cheques, a security deposit and AED 177.75 for Ejari | The deposit, plus about 7% of the price in fees on a ready home |
| Flexibility | At least 90 days' notice on either side to change terms or not renew | Selling needs a transfer and the developer's NOC |
| Residency | No property visa | A two-year investor visa, or a Golden Visa from AED 2 million |

### Areas by commute

- **Dubai Marina.** Apartments on the Red Line at Sobha Realty and DMCC stations, with the tram along the waterfront
- **Downtown Dubai and Business Bay.** Apartments in the centre, each with its own Red Line station: Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall and Business Bay
- **Dubai Hills Estate.** Villas and apartments around the golf course; no Metro station, with RTA bus DH1 to Equiti station on the Red Line
- **Jumeirah Village Circle.** Lower-priced apartments and townhouses; no Metro station, with bus J01 to Mall of the Emirates
- **Dubai Creek Harbour.** New waterfront apartments; the Metro Blue Line, with a station here, is due to open on 9 September 2029

Each [area guide](https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/) has the homes, the transport and our price data; we mark the school commute for each shortlisted home.

### What a non-resident needs

- **To rent:** your passport, your visa status and a UAE bank account, because by market practice rent cheques are drawn on a UAE bank
- **To buy:** a valid passport, which identifies you at the registration trustee. If you cannot attend, an attorney signs under a power of attorney notarised abroad, legalised, attested, translated into Arabic and issued within two years

### For companies moving staff

We run one brief for a whole team: a shortlist per household, grouped viewings on a visit or by video, and one point of contact for the people team. Tenancy terms, cheques and deposits are negotiated to match your relocation policy.

A timeline is set back from each arrival date: contract and Ejari first, then DEWA and keys. Where the move is permanent, the same adviser handles the purchase later; [buying a home in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/services/buying-property-in-dubai/) sets out that process.

### What it costs

Finding a rental home carries a fee agreed in writing before you sign; buying carries the customary 2% plus VAT on a resale and nothing extra on an off-plan purchase from a developer.

### Questions

**Should I rent or buy when I move to Dubai?**
Most people rent first. A tenancy can be in place within weeks and can be left with at least 90 days' notice at expiry, while a purchase carries about 7% in fees on a ready home.

**Can I rent a home before I arrive?**
Yes. We view by video, negotiate the terms, check the landlord's title deed and prepare the contract so it is ready to sign and register on Ejari when you land.

**Do I need a residence visa to buy a home in Dubai?**
No. Buyers of any nationality can own freehold property in Dubai's designated areas, and a valid passport identifies a non-resident at the registration trustee.

**Which areas are best for commuting?**
Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai and Business Bay each have a Red Line Metro station; Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Village Circle rely on bus links; Dubai Creek Harbour gets a Blue Line station when the line opens on 9 September 2029.

**What is Ejari and do I need it to connect utilities?**
Ejari is the system for registering a tenancy with RERA, required by Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 and costing AED 177.75 online. The certificate is the proof of address used when the DEWA account is opened in your name.

**Can you move a whole team?**
Yes. One brief covers every household, with a shortlist per family, grouped viewings and one contact for your people team.

## Buying a home in Dubai: the process from start to keys

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/how-to-buy-property-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-09-15

Who can own, what to budget, which forms you sign, and what happens at the registration trustee when the home becomes yours.

### In short

- Anyone can buy freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold areas, whatever their nationality, and a UAE residence visa is not required.
- Plan for about 7% on top of the price of a ready home. That covers the 4% DLD transfer fee, the customary 2% agency fee plus VAT, and the trustee, title deed and NOC fees.
- You and the seller sign Form F, the DLD's standard sale contract, and by custom you pay a 10% deposit at that point.
- The home becomes yours at a DLD registration trustee office, where the seller is paid and your title deed is issued.

### Who can buy property in Dubai

Dubai lets buyers of every nationality own property outright in its designated freehold areas. Regulation No. 3 of 2006 listed the first of these areas, and the list has grown since. Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Palm Jumeirah, Business Bay, Dubai Hills Estate, Jumeirah Village Circle and Dubai Creek Harbour are all on it. Our [area guides](https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/) cover each of them.

Under Dubai Law No. 7 of 2006, a non-UAE national may hold freehold title in a designated area with no time limit, or a leasehold right of up to 99 years. Outside the designated areas the rules differ, so confirm that an area is freehold before you make an offer.

You do not have to live in the UAE. A non-resident buyer identifies themselves with a valid passport at the registration trustee. If you cannot attend in person, an attorney can sign for you under a power of attorney. One issued abroad must be notarised, legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate, attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, translated into Arabic and less than two years old. [Buying property in Dubai from abroad](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-property-in-dubai-from-abroad/) walks through it.

### Setting a budget that includes the fees

The price is not the whole number. On a ready home, the fees come to about 7% of the price. Fix your budget with those fees inside it from the start.

- **DLD transfer fee:** 4% of the price, paid by the buyer by custom
- **Title deed fees:** AED 520 for an apartment or villa
- **Registration trustee fee:** AED 4,000 plus VAT, or AED 2,000 plus VAT when the price is under AED 500,000
- **Agency fee:** usually 2% of the price plus VAT
- **Developer NOC:** AED 500 to 5,000, set by the developer

The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) gives the full figure for any price, and [the cost of buying property in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai/) explains each line.

What ExpertCare does for you here: before a viewing, your adviser gives you the price and the DLD, trustee and agency fees together, so the figure you plan around is the figure you will pay.

### Appointing a broker and checking adverts

Form B is RERA's standard contract between a buyer and a broker. It records what the broker will do for you and the commission you will pay. Sign it before the broker starts work, so the terms are on paper.

Every property advert in Dubai must carry a Trakheesi advertising permit number, together with the brokerage's office registration number (ORN) and the broker's registration number (BRN). Printed and video adverts have carried a Madmoun QR code since 24 April 2023. Scan it and the Dubai Land Department confirms whether the advert is valid.

What ExpertCare does for you here: if a home cannot be advertised legally, we do not show it. The adviser who shows you a home stays with you through the offer, the transfer and the handover.

### The steps from offer to title deed

1. **Make your offer.** Your broker puts the offer to the seller's side. Agree the price, the deposit, the transfer date and who pays the developer's NOC fee.
2. **Sign Form F.** Form F is RERA's standard sale contract between buyer and seller, often called the MOU. It records the price, the deposit and the date of transfer. By custom you pay a 10% deposit when you sign, and it is held until the transfer.
3. **Obtain the developer's NOC.** The developer of the building issues a no-objection certificate confirming it does not object to the transfer. The fee is AED 500 to 5,000, set by the developer, and Form F records who pays it.
4. **Transfer at a registration trustee.** Buyer and seller, or their attorneys, meet at a Dubai Land Department registration trustee office. The seller is paid, the fees are settled and the sale is registered.
5. **Collect your title deed.** The title deed is issued in your name.

### What happens on transfer day

The transfer is the moment ownership passes. It takes place at a Dubai Land Department registration trustee office, an approved office that handles the registration on DLD's behalf.

- The seller receives the balance of the price
- You pay the 4% transfer fee and the AED 520 title deed fees to the Dubai Land Department
- You pay the trustee's fee: AED 4,000 plus VAT, or AED 2,000 plus VAT when the price is under AED 500,000
- The sale is registered and the title deed is issued in your name

Bring your passport. If an attorney attends for you, they bring the original power of attorney in the form the Dubai Land Department accepts.

### Buying off-plan instead

A home bought from a developer before the building is complete follows a different route. You reserve, sign the developer's sale agreement, pay in instalments into the project's escrow account, and register the purchase on the Oqood system for 4% of the price plus AED 20. There is no Form F with a private seller and no developer NOC on a first sale.

[Buying off-plan in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-off-plan-in-dubai/) covers the whole process, and [off-plan or ready](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/off-plan-vs-ready-property-in-dubai/) helps you choose between the two.

### What ExpertCare does for you

- **Before you view:** the price and every fee together, so you know the whole number first
- **During the search:** only homes that can be advertised legally, and one adviser from the first viewing to the keys
- **At the offer:** the offer, Form F and the transfer date handled with the seller's side
- **After the deal:** if you plan to let the home, the same team finds the tenant and handles rent collection, maintenance and renewals

Every figure in this guide comes from the sources listed at the end. The [facts page](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-facts/) gathers them in one place.

### Questions

**Can a foreigner buy property in Dubai?**
Yes. Buyers of any nationality can own freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold areas, which were first listed in Regulation No. 3 of 2006 and include Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Palm Jumeirah and Dubai Hills Estate. A UAE residence visa is not required.

**What is Form F?**
Form F is RERA's standard sale contract between a buyer and a seller, often called the MOU. It records the price, the deposit, the transfer date and who pays the developer's NOC fee.

**How much deposit do I pay when I sign Form F?**
By custom, 10% of the price. It is market practice rather than a legal requirement, and the deposit is held until the transfer.

**What is Form B?**
Form B is RERA's standard contract between a buyer and a broker. It sets out what the broker does for you and the commission you pay.

**How much are the fees when buying property in Dubai?**
About 7% of the price on a ready home: the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT, the customary 2% agency fee plus VAT, and the developer's NOC fee of AED 500 to 5,000.

**Where does the transfer take place?**
At a Dubai Land Department registration trustee office. Buyer and seller, or their attorneys, meet there. The seller is paid, the fees are settled, the sale is registered and the title deed is issued in the buyer's name.

**Do I need to be in Dubai to buy?**
No. A non-resident buyer identifies themselves with a valid passport at the registration trustee, and an attorney can sign under a power of attorney that has been notarised, legalised, attested, translated into Arabic and issued within the last two years.

**How do I check that a property advert is genuine?**
Look for the Trakheesi permit number and the brokerage's ORN and broker's BRN. Printed and video adverts carry a Madmoun QR code. Scan it to confirm the advert with the Dubai Land Department.

### Sources

## The cost of buying property in Dubai, fee by fee

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-09-15

What the Dubai Land Department charges, what the broker and developer charge, who pays each one, and a worked example at AED 2,000,000.

### In short

- On a ready home, fees add about 7% to the price. The largest is the Dubai Land Department transfer fee of 4%, which by custom the buyer pays in full.
- Fixed DLD fees are AED 520 for the title deed and AED 4,000 plus VAT for the registration trustee, or AED 2,000 plus VAT below AED 500,000. The customary agency fee is 2% plus VAT, and the developer's NOC costs AED 500 to 5,000.
- At AED 2,000,000 the fees total about AED 131,720, or 6.6% of the price.
- Off-plan homes pay 4% plus AED 20 on Oqood.

### Fees on a ready home

A ready home is one that is built and has a title deed. When you buy one from its owner, five fees apply. Three go to the Dubai Land Department or its registration trustee, one to your broker and one to the developer of the building.

| Fee | Amount | Who sets it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transfer fee | 4% of the price | Dubai Land Department |
| Title deed fees | AED 520 for an apartment or villa: AED 250 for the title deed, AED 250 for the unit, AED 10 knowledge fee and AED 10 innovation fee | Dubai Land Department |
| Registration trustee fee | AED 4,000 plus VAT at AED 500,000 and above; AED 2,000 plus VAT below | Dubai Land Department |
| Agency fee | Usually 2% of the price plus VAT | Market custom, agreed with your broker |
| Developer NOC | AED 500 to 5,000 | The developer |

VAT in the UAE is 5%. It is added to the trustee fee and the agency fee. The transfer fee and the title deed fees are shown without it.

The transfer fee is a percentage, so it scales with the price. The title deed and trustee fees are fixed, so they weigh more on a cheaper home. That is why the total sits a little under 7% at AED 2,000,000 and a little over it on a smaller purchase: at AED 1,000,000 the same five fees come to about AED 70,720, or 7.1%.

### Who pays which fee

By custom the buyer pays the whole 4% transfer fee. The Dubai Land Department's own fee schedule splits it equally between buyer and seller, so a different split is possible if both sides agree to it in Form F, the sale contract.

- **Transfer fee:** the buyer, by custom
- **Title deed and trustee fees:** settled at the transfer; our calculator shows them against the buyer
- **Agency fee:** agreed between you and your broker. 2% plus VAT is the customary rate, not a legal one
- **Developer NOC:** whoever Form F says. Agree it before you sign

If you are selling, the same fees apply. By custom your buyer pays the transfer fee, and your own agency fee is agreed in writing before the home is listed.

The NOC matters to both sides. Under Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 a home may not be sold while its service charges are unpaid, so a seller settles them before the developer issues the certificate. Agree in Form F who pays the NOC fee, and ask for the figure before you sign rather than at the transfer.

### A worked example at AED 2,000,000

Take a ready apartment at AED 2,000,000. The price is above AED 500,000, so the higher trustee fee applies. The NOC is shown at the top of the developer's range.

| Fee | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| DLD transfer fee | AED 80,000 |
| DLD title deed fees | AED 520 |
| Registration trustee fee | AED 4,200 |
| Agency fee | AED 42,000 |
| Developer NOC | AED 5,000 |
| Price plus fees | AED 2,131,720 |

The fees come to about AED 131,720, which is 6.6% of the price. The calculator further down runs the same sum for any price.

### Fees on an off-plan home

A home bought from the developer before completion is registered on the Dubai Land Department's Oqood system rather than transferred at a trustee. The fee is the same 4% of the price, plus AED 10 knowledge and AED 10 innovation fees. At AED 2,000,000 that is AED 80,000 plus AED 20.

- **No trustee or title deed fee at this stage.** Our calculator shows only the Oqood fee and the AED 20 admin fees on an off-plan purchase. The title deed is issued once the project has its completion certificate
- **No developer NOC.** There is no previous owner on a first sale from the developer
- **Developer administration fees.** Some developers charge their own, and they vary. Ask for them in writing before you reserve

[Buying off-plan in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-off-plan-in-dubai/) covers the payment plan, the escrow account that holds your instalments, and the checks to make before you reserve.

### Work out your costs

Calculator: https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/

### Costs once you own

Owning carries running costs that are not part of the purchase but belong in the same budget.

- **Service charges:** an annual charge for the upkeep of shared areas in a managed building or community. The rate differs by building. Under Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 it needs RERA's approval on a budget approved by a certified audit firm, and a home cannot be sold while its service charges are unpaid. See [service charges in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/service-charges-in-dubai/)
- **Income tax:** the UAE does not levy income tax on individuals. Rental income from property held in your own name is not subject to corporate tax when the activity does not require a licence, under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023
- **VAT on letting:** residential leases are generally exempt. The first supply of a new residential property within three years of completion is zero-rated
- **Moving and furnishing:** there is no official figure. Budget for them alongside the fees

Ask for the current service charge on any home you consider, and ask before you make the offer rather than after.

### How ExpertCare shows the cost

When you ask about a home, we give you the price and the Dubai Land Department, trustee and agency fees together, before you book a viewing. The figures come from the same sources as this guide, and the [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) lets you run any price, ready or off-plan. If a home needs a developer NOC, who pays it is settled before Form F is signed, not after.

Owners who let through us get the same approach after the purchase: rent collection, maintenance and renewals handled by the team that found the tenant, with the costs set out before you commit. [Renting out property in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/renting-out-property-in-dubai/) explains the rules a landlord works under.

### Questions

**How much does it cost to buy property in Dubai?**
About 7% of the price on a ready home. The 4% DLD transfer fee is the largest part. The rest is AED 520 in title deed fees, the trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT, the customary 2% agency fee plus VAT and the developer's NOC of AED 500 to 5,000. At AED 2,000,000 the total is about AED 131,720.

**Who pays the 4% DLD transfer fee?**
The buyer, by custom. The Dubai Land Department's own schedule divides the fee equally between buyer and seller, so the two sides can agree a different split in Form F.

**What are the DLD title deed fees?**
AED 520 for an apartment or villa: AED 250 for the title deed, AED 250 for the unit, and AED 10 each in knowledge and innovation fees.

**What is the registration trustee fee?**
AED 4,000 plus VAT when the price is AED 500,000 or more, and AED 2,000 plus VAT below that. The trustee is the DLD-approved office where the transfer takes place.

**Is the agency fee fixed by law?**
No. 2% of the price plus VAT is the customary rate in Dubai. The commission is agreed between you and your broker.

**What fees does an off-plan purchase carry?**
4% of the price to register on Oqood, plus AED 10 knowledge and AED 10 innovation fees, and any administration charge the developer sets. There is no developer NOC on a first sale from the developer.

**What tax do you pay on property you own in Dubai?**
The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals. Rental income from property held in your own name is not subject to corporate tax when the activity does not require a licence, under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023. Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT.

### Sources

- [Dubai Land Department: property sale registration](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/)
- [Dubai Land Department: registering the initial (off-plan) sale](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-to-register-the-initial-sale/)
- [Property Finder: DLD fees in Dubai (2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/dld-fees-dubai/)
- [Bayut: the cost of buying property in Dubai](https://www.bayut.com/mybayut/cost-buying-property-dubai/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 6 of 2019 on jointly owned real property](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2019/Law%20No.%20(6)%20of%202019%20Concerning%20Ownership%20of%20Jointly%20Owned%20Real%20Property%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)
- [UAE Government portal: taxation](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment/taxation)
- [Federal Tax Authority: real estate investment for natural persons (October 2024)](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2024/Real-Estate-Investment-for-natural-persons-22-10-2024.pdf)
- [UAE Ministry of Finance: value added tax](https://mof.gov.ae/en/public-finance/tax/value-added-tax-vat/)
