## Buying off-plan in Dubai: how it works and what to check

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-off-plan-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-09-15

Payment plans, the escrow law behind every instalment, Oqood registration, what an advert must show, and handover.

### In short

- When you buy off-plan in Dubai, every payment goes into an escrow account opened for that project under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007, and the money can be used only to build it.
- The sale is registered on the Dubai Land Department's Oqood system for 4% of the price plus AED 20, before a title deed exists.
- Each off-plan advert needs a Trakheesi permit for the unit and must show the developer, the escrow account number and the expected completion date.

### What buying off-plan means

An off-plan home is one you buy from the developer before the building is complete, sometimes before construction starts. You do not pay the price at a transfer. You pay in stages set by a payment plan: a first payment at reservation, instalments as the building rises, and the balance at handover or after it.

Payment plans differ from one developer to the next. Some ask for most of the price during construction, and some leave a larger share to handover or after it. The plan is part of the sale agreement, so read it as closely as the price.

Because there is no title deed yet, the protections differ from a resale. Two matter most: the escrow account that holds your money, and the Oqood register that records you as the buyer. [Off-plan or ready](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/off-plan-vs-ready-property-in-dubai/) weighs the two routes against each other.

### Where your money is held

Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 requires a developer to open an escrow account for each project with an approved escrow agent. Buyers' payments go into that account and may be spent only on building that project. The developer's creditors cannot seize the money.

The escrow account number must appear on every off-plan advert. Check that the number in your sale agreement matches the one on the advert, and make every payment to that account. Keep the receipt for each instalment, because the record of your payments is what shows you have met your obligations when the unit is registered in your name.

> Never pay an off-plan instalment into a personal account, a broker's account or any account other than the project's escrow account. The protection in Law No. 8 of 2007 applies to money in that account.

### Registering your purchase on Oqood

Oqood is the Dubai Land Department's register of off-plan sales. Once your purchase is registered, DLD's records show you as the buyer of that unit, even though the title deed will not exist until the building is complete.

- **Oqood fee:** 4% of the price, the same rate as the transfer fee on a ready home
- **Admin fees:** AED 10 knowledge fee and AED 10 innovation fee
- **Developer charges:** some developers add their own administration fee. Ask for it in writing before you reserve
- **No NOC:** a first sale from the developer carries no developer NOC fee

Once the project has its completion certificate, the developer must register the sold units in the names of the buyers who have met their obligations, under Article 8 of Dubai Law No. 13 of 2008. That is when your title deed is issued. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) shows the off-plan fees for any price.

### What an off-plan advert must show

Dubai's advertising rules ask more of an off-plan advert than of a resale advert. Before you take one seriously, look for all of these.

- A Trakheesi advertising permit number. Since April 2024 each off-plan unit needs its own permit, not only the project
- The developer's name
- The project's escrow account number
- The expected completion date
- A Madmoun QR code on printed and video adverts, which you scan to confirm the advert with the Dubai Land Department
- The brokerage's ORN and the broker's BRN, as on every property advert

If an advert leaves out any of these, ask for them before you pay anything.

### Checks before you reserve

1. **The developer and the project.** Confirm the developer's name and that the project is registered with the Dubai Land Department with an escrow account.
2. **The escrow account number.** Match it between the advert, the sale agreement and the payment instructions.
3. **The payment plan.** Read each instalment: the amount, and whether a date or a stage of construction triggers it.
4. **The completion date and the delay terms.** Note the expected completion date on the advert, and read what the sale agreement says if the developer is late.
5. **Every fee.** The 4% Oqood fee and AED 20 in admin fees, any developer administration charge, and the service charge once the building is handed over.
6. **What happens if you cannot pay.** Under Law No. 13 of 2008 as amended by Law No. 19 of 2020, a developer may keep up to 40% of the unit's value if the project is more than 60% complete, or up to 25% below that, when a buyer defaults. Know this before you commit to a plan.

What ExpertCare does for you here: we give you the developer, permit and escrow details and the payment plan, with the Oqood fee and the service charge beside it, so you see the whole number before you reserve. The same adviser stays with you to handover.

### Handover and defects

At handover you inspect the home, settle what the payment plan says is due, and receive the keys. Your title deed follows once the developer registers the unit after the completion certificate. From that point the home is a ready home: if you sell it later, the buyer pays the 4% transfer fee by custom and the transfer takes place at a registration trustee.

- The developer must repair or replace defective installations for one year from handover, under Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019
- The developer must fix structural defects for ten years from the completion certificate, under the same article
- Service charges apply once the building is handed over. Ask for the figure before you reserve, not at handover

[Handover and snagging in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/handover-and-snagging-in-dubai/) explains the inspection and what belongs on the snag list.

### Off-plan and the Golden Visa

The Dubai Land Department's and GDRFA Dubai's pages on the property Golden Visa do not say whether an off-plan home counts towards the AED 2 million threshold. If the visa is part of your reason to buy, confirm the position with GDRFA before you reserve. [The Golden Visa through property](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/golden-visa-through-property/) sets out the published rules.

### Questions

**Is my money safe when I buy off-plan in Dubai?**
Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 requires off-plan payments to go into an escrow account opened for the project, to be spent only on building it, and the developer's creditors cannot seize it. The protection applies to money paid into that account, so pay nowhere else.

**What is Oqood?**
Oqood is the Dubai Land Department's register for off-plan sales. It records you as the buyer before a title deed exists. The fee is 4% of the price plus AED 20.

**How much are the fees on an off-plan purchase?**
4% of the price plus AED 20 to the Dubai Land Department for Oqood registration, and any administration charge the developer sets. There is no developer NOC on a first sale from the developer.

**What must an off-plan advert in Dubai show?**
A Trakheesi permit for the unit, the developer's name, the project's escrow account number and the expected completion date, plus a Madmoun QR code on printed and video adverts.

**What happens if I cannot keep up with the payment plan?**
Under Law No. 13 of 2008 as amended by Law No. 19 of 2020, the developer may keep up to 40% of the unit's value on a project more than 60% complete, or up to 25% on one below that.

**How long is a developer liable for defects?**
One year from handover for defective installations, and ten years from the completion certificate for structural defects, under Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019.

**Does an off-plan home count for the Golden Visa?**
The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai pages on the property Golden Visa do not address off-plan homes. Confirm with GDRFA before you buy with the visa in mind.

### Sources

- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 8 of 2007 on escrow accounts](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2007/Law%20No.%20(8)%20of%202007.html)
- [Dubai Land Department: registering the initial (off-plan) sale](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-to-register-the-initial-sale/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 13 of 2008 on the interim property register](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2008/Law%20No.%20(13)%20of%202008.html)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 19 of 2020 amending Law No. 13 of 2008](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2020/Law%20No.%20(19)%20of%202020%20Amending%20Law%20No.%20(13)%20of%202008%20Regulating%20the%20Interim%20Real%20Property%20Register%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 6 of 2019 on jointly owned real property](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2019/Law%20No.%20(6)%20of%202019%20Concerning%20Ownership%20of%20Jointly%20Owned%20Real%20Property%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)
- [Bayut: Trakheesi advertising permits (August 2026)](https://www.bayut.com/mybayut/trakheesi/)
- [Property Finder: Trakheesi permits (January 2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/trakheesi/)
- [Dubai Land Department: Madmoun QR codes on property adverts (April 2023)](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/news-media/dubai-land-department-provides-madmoun-service-to-verify-validity-of-real-estate-ads-via-qr-codes/)
- [Dubai Land Department: Golden Visa for property investors](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-for-golden-visa-investor/)
- [GDRFA Dubai: Golden Visa for property investors](https://www.gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/8ea80da4-f43e-11eb-0320-0050569629e8)

## The Golden Visa through property in Dubai

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/golden-visa-through-property/
Updated: 2026-09-16

The AED 2 million threshold, how a co-owner changes the count, the silence on off-plan, the two-year investor visa below the line, and where to apply.

### In short

- Property in Dubai worth AED 2 million or more, in one home or several, lets an investor apply for a Golden Visa. The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai describe it as ten years and renewable; the federal portal shows a different term.
- A jointly owned home counts only when your own share is worth AED 2 million.
- Below AED 2 million, DLD lists a two-year investor residence visa: any value for a sole owner, or a share of at least AED 400,000 for a joint owner.
- In April 2026 GDRFA Dubai and DLD agreed to move property residency services into GDRFA Dubai's system, so confirm the channel and the fees when you apply.

### The AED 2 million threshold

The rule is a value, not a number of homes. Property worth at least AED 2 million makes a property investor in Dubai eligible to apply for a Golden Visa. One home at AED 2 million qualifies, and so do two homes worth AED 1 million each.

The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai describe the visa as ten years and renewable. The federal government portal shows a different term for property investors. The sources do not agree, so confirm the term with GDRFA when you apply rather than planning around either figure.

- **Minimum value:** AED 2 million, in one property or several
- **Term:** ten years, renewable, according to DLD and GDRFA Dubai
- **Jointly owned property:** counts only when the applicant's own share is worth AED 2 million or more
- **Off-plan property:** not addressed on the official pages

### Homes owned with someone else

If you co-own a home, GDRFA Dubai counts only your own share, and that share must itself be worth AED 2 million or more. A couple who own a home worth AED 3 million in equal halves each hold AED 1.5 million, so neither qualifies on that home alone.

On the published rule, a co-owner qualifies when their own share reaches AED 2 million, whatever the other shares are worth. Two people who hold a home worth AED 4 million in equal halves each hold AED 2 million, so each meets the threshold on that home. Decide how a home will be held before the transfer, because the title deed records the shares.

### Off-plan homes

Neither the Dubai Land Department's service page nor GDRFA Dubai's says whether an off-plan home counts towards the threshold. Off-plan is where an answer would matter most, since instalments are paid over years before a title deed exists.

Do not rely on an off-plan purchase for the visa until GDRFA confirms the position in writing. [Buying off-plan in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-off-plan-in-dubai/) covers the purchase itself.

### Below AED 2 million: the two-year investor visa

For property under the threshold, the Dubai Land Department's service page lists a two-year investor residence visa. A sole owner qualifies with a property of any value. A joint owner needs a share worth at least AED 400,000.

| Visa | Property | Term | Fee listed by DLD |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Golden Visa | AED 2 million or more, in one property or several | Ten years, renewable, according to DLD and GDRFA Dubai | AED 9,884.75 for the main applicant |
| Investor residence visa | Any value for a sole owner; a share of AED 400,000 or more for a joint owner | Two years | AED 10,212.50 |

Both services have been run by the Dubai Land Department for property owners, and the fees above are the ones DLD lists. They may change when the services move to GDRFA Dubai.

The investor visa fee DLD lists, AED 10,212.50, is higher than the Golden Visa fee it lists for the main applicant, AED 9,884.75. The fee is not what separates the two routes. The property value and the term are.

### The purchase behind the visa

The visa follows the property, so the purchase comes first and runs as any other does. You can buy freehold in Dubai's designated freehold areas whatever your nationality, and you do not need a residence visa to buy. [How to buy a home in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/how-to-buy-property-in-dubai/) sets out each step.

- **The fees.** On a ready home at AED 2,000,000, the fees are about AED 131,720: the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT, the customary 2% agency fee plus VAT and the developer's NOC. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) runs any price
- **The title deed.** It is issued in your name at the registration trustee and records your share of the home. It is the document that shows what you own
- **Several homes.** The threshold can be met across more than one property, so two smaller homes can add up to it

Buying off-plan to reach the threshold is the one route the official pages do not confirm. Treat it as open until GDRFA answers in writing.

### Where to apply and what it costs

The Dubai Land Department has handled the Golden Visa and the investor visa for property owners, and lists the Golden Visa fee for the main applicant as AED 9,884.75. In April 2026 GDRFA Dubai and DLD agreed to move property residency services into GDRFA Dubai's system.

Because the channel is changing, check three things before you apply: where to submit the application, which documents it needs, and the fee on the day.

> ExpertCare does not give immigration advice. Decisions on visas rest with the UAE authorities. Confirm every requirement with GDRFA Dubai before you buy with the visa in mind.

### If the visa is part of why you are buying

1. **Fix the value, not the count.** Add up the homes you will own. The total must reach AED 2 million, counting only your own share of any co-owned home.
2. **Check the term with GDRFA.** The official pages disagree on it. Ask before you plan around ten years.
3. **Treat off-plan as unconfirmed.** The official pages are silent. Get a written answer first.
4. **Confirm the channel and the fee.** The services are moving from DLD to GDRFA Dubai, and the published fees may change with them.

What ExpertCare does for you here: when you tell us the visa matters, we search at or above the threshold, show the value of your share on any co-owned home, and point you to the published DLD and GDRFA rules. The application itself is yours to make with GDRFA Dubai.

### Questions

**How much property do I need for a Golden Visa in Dubai?**
Property worth AED 2 million or more. The value can come from one property or several.

**How long is the Golden Visa for property investors?**
The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai describe it as ten years and renewable. The federal government portal shows a different term for property investors, so confirm it with GDRFA when you apply.

**Can co-owners add their shares together?**
No. GDRFA Dubai counts a jointly owned property only when the applicant's own share is worth AED 2 million or more.

**Does an off-plan property count towards the Golden Visa?**
The official Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai pages do not say. Get a written answer from GDRFA before you buy off-plan with the visa in mind.

**Is there a residence visa for property under AED 2 million?**
The Dubai Land Department lists a two-year investor residence visa. A sole owner qualifies with property of any value, and a joint owner needs a share worth at least AED 400,000. DLD lists the fee as AED 10,212.50.

**Where do I apply for the property Golden Visa?**
The Dubai Land Department has run the service and lists the fee for the main applicant as AED 9,884.75. In April 2026 GDRFA Dubai and DLD agreed to move property residency services into GDRFA Dubai's system, so check the current channel before you apply.

### Sources

- [Dubai Land Department: Golden Visa for property investors](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-for-golden-visa-investor/)
- [Dubai Land Department: investor visa for property owners](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-for-investor-visa/)
- [GDRFA Dubai: Golden Visa for property investors](https://www.gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/8ea80da4-f43e-11eb-0320-0050569629e8)
- [Dubai Media Office: GDRFA Dubai and DLD residency services (April 2026)](https://mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2026/april/11-04/gdrfa)
- [UAE Government portal: Golden Visa](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-visas/golden-visa)
- [Dubai Land Department: property sale registration](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/)

## Off-plan or ready: which suits you in Dubai

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/off-plan-vs-ready-property-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-09-16

The same decision from both sides: what you pay and when, where your money sits, and when you get the keys.

### In short

- With a ready home you pay the price at transfer and can move in or let it the same day. With an off-plan home you pay in instalments while the developer builds it.
- The Dubai Land Department takes 4% on both. On a ready home that is the transfer fee; on an off-plan home it is the Oqood registration fee.
- Every instalment you pay the developer goes into the project's escrow account under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007.

### What ready and off-plan mean

A ready home exists. It has a title deed, a service charge history and, often, a tenant or a previous owner. You buy it from that owner, through a Dubai Land Department registration trustee, and you own it from the day of transfer.

An off-plan home does not exist yet, or is still being built. You buy it from the developer against plans and a specification. The sale is recorded on the Dubai Land Department's Oqood register, and a title deed is issued once the building has its completion certificate and you have met your obligations under the sale agreement.

### The two compared

|  | Ready home | Off-plan home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When you pay | A deposit on Form F, by custom 10%, then the balance at transfer | In instalments fixed by the payment plan, during construction and at or after handover |
| Dubai Land Department fee | 4% transfer fee and AED 520 in title deed fees | 4% Oqood registration and AED 20 in admin fees |
| Other fees | Registration trustee fee, agency fee, the developer's NOC fee | Whatever administration charge the developer sets |
| Where the money goes | To the seller, at transfer | Into the project's escrow account |
| Living in it or letting it | From the day of transfer | After handover |
| What you can see first | The home, the building and the neighbours | Drawings, a specification and sometimes a show apartment |

Timing decides most cases. If you need the home this year, a ready home is the better fit.

### How the payments differ

On a ready home the money moves twice. By custom you pay a 10% deposit when you and the seller sign Form F, the sale contract. You pay the rest at the registration trustee office on transfer day, usually by manager's cheque.

On an off-plan home the developer's payment plan sets the dates. Some plans ask for a share at reservation, instalments tied to construction milestones, and a final share at handover. Others carry part of the price past handover. Each instalment is paid into the escrow account, not to the developer's general account.

- Read the plan for what triggers each instalment: a date, or a construction stage
- Ask what happens if a milestone slips: whether the instalment moves with it
- Add the 4% Oqood fee to your first payments, because it is due at registration

### The fees on each

On a ready home the Dubai Land Department charges 4% of the price, plus AED 520 in title deed fees for an apartment or villa. The registration trustee charges AED 4,000 plus VAT when the price is AED 500,000 or more, and AED 2,000 plus VAT below that. The agency fee is 2% plus VAT by custom. The developer's no-objection certificate costs AED 500 to 5,000, set by the developer, and Form F records who pays it.

On an off-plan home bought from the developer, the Dubai Land Department charges the same 4% to register the sale on Oqood, plus AED 10 knowledge and AED 10 innovation fees. There is no NOC on a first sale from the developer. Any other charge is the developer's own administration fee, so ask for it in writing. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) shows both sets of fees at any price.

### Where your money sits

When you buy a ready home, the price goes to the seller at transfer and the title deed is issued to you in the same sitting. The exchange is simultaneous, which is the point of the trustee office.

When you buy off-plan, Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 requires every payment to go into an escrow account opened for that project. The money can be used only to build that project, and the developer's creditors cannot seize it. The account number must appear on the project's adverts, and you can ask the developer for it before you pay a dirham.

### Which to choose

A ready home fits when:

- You want to live in it, or earn rent from it, within weeks
- You want to walk through the exact home, and see the building, before you commit

An off-plan home fits when:

- You would rather pay in stages over the build than all at once
- You want a new home in a district that is still taking shape
- You can wait for handover, and your plans can absorb a delay

### Questions to settle first

1. **On a ready home: the condition, the service charge and the price.** Compare the asking price with recent sales of similar homes in the same building or community, and read the service charge before you judge the return.
2. **On an off-plan home: the developer, the escrow account and the plan.** Check the project is registered, confirm the escrow account, and read what the sale agreement says about delays and what each instalment is tied to.
3. **On either: the total cost, not the price.** Fees differ between the two, and the [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) puts them side by side. [Buying off-plan in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-off-plan-in-dubai/) lists the off-plan checks in full.

If you cannot answer one of these for a home you like, find the answer before you commit.

### Questions

**Is an off-plan home cheaper than a ready one in Dubai?**
Not by rule. The developer sets an off-plan price and the resale market sets a ready price, so compare the price per square foot of similar homes in the same area. Remember too that an off-plan home earns nothing until handover.

**Do I pay the 4% DLD fee on both?**
Yes. On a ready home it is the 4% transfer fee plus AED 520 in title deed fees and the registration trustee fee. On an off-plan home it is 4% to register the sale on Oqood plus AED 20.

**Is there a developer NOC when I buy off-plan from the developer?**
No. The NOC is needed on a resale, when a developer confirms the seller has no outstanding dues. On a first sale from the developer there is nothing to confirm.

**Where do my off-plan payments go?**
Into an escrow account opened for the project. Under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 the money may be used only to build that project, and the developer's creditors cannot touch it.

**When can I move into or let each type of home?**
A ready home from the day of transfer, when the title deed is issued in your name. An off-plan home after handover, once the building is complete and you have paid what is due.

**What can I inspect before buying off-plan?**
The drawings, the specification and, where the developer has built one, a show apartment. On a ready home you inspect the home itself, so a ready purchase carries less uncertainty about what you get.

### Sources

- [Dubai Land Department: property sale registration](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/)
- [Dubai Land Department: registering the initial (off-plan) sale](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-to-register-the-initial-sale/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 8 of 2007 on escrow accounts](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2007/Law%20No.%20(8)%20of%202007.html)
- [Meraas: guide to Form F (April 2026)](https://meraas.com/en/latest-post/journal/complete-guide-form-f-dubai)
- [Property Finder: DLD fees in Dubai (2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/dld-fees-dubai/)

## How to buy property in Dubai when you live abroad

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-property-in-dubai-from-abroad/
Updated: 2026-09-16

What changes when you are not in the UAE: the documents, the power of attorney rules, moving the money, visas and tax.

### In short

- A non-resident can own freehold property in Dubai's designated areas, and a valid passport is all the identification the registration trustee needs.
- If you cannot be in Dubai, an attorney can sign for you. A power of attorney issued abroad must be notarised there, legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate, attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, translated into Arabic and dated within the last two years.
- DLD's fully digital sale runs on Emirates ID, UAE Pass and a UAE bank account, so non-residents complete at a trustee office.
- Owning property can bring a two-year investor residence visa, or a Golden Visa from AED 2 million.

### Can a non-resident buy in Dubai

Yes. Dubai Law No. 7 of 2006 lets non-UAE nationals hold freehold property without a time limit, or leasehold rights of up to 99 years, in the areas designated for it. Those areas were first listed in 2006 and have grown since; every community in our [area guides](https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/) is one of them. You do not need a residence visa, a local sponsor or a UAE company to buy.

This guide covers an individual buying in their own name. A company buying through its licence has its own document list at the trustee, and a foreign company needs more of it.

### What identification you need

The Dubai Land Department registers sales through registration trustee offices. A UAE resident shows an Emirates ID. A non-resident foreigner shows a valid passport. That is the whole identification requirement at the trustee.

On a resale in a freehold area the trustee also needs the developer's electronic no-objection certificate. The seller applies for it through the Dubai REST app, and it confirms the seller has paid the developer what is due. The sale contract, Form F, sets out who pays the NOC fee.

### Buying without flying in

You can give someone a power of attorney to sign for you. DLD Circular No. 29/R/2025, as summarised by Dubai law firms, sets the standard for a power of attorney issued outside the UAE. It must be:

- Notarised by the competent authority in the country of issue
- Legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate in that country
- Attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs
- Produced as the original, not a copy or a scan
- Translated in full into Arabic by a UAE-licensed translator, where it is in another language
- Dated within the two years before it is used

A power of attorney notarised inside the UAE and entered in the electronic register generally stays valid unless it states an end date. Whichever route you use, the document must name the transaction. General wording is rejected at the trustee, so have it drafted for this purchase, naming the property if you already know it.

Choose the attorney with care. A lawyer, a relative in the UAE or the brokerage can act, and the power of attorney can be limited to signing the contract and the transfer, with no authority over the money.

### Getting the money to Dubai

DLD takes its own fees by ePay, Dubai Pay, the Noqodi wallet or manager's cheque. The price itself is a matter between you and the seller. By market practice it is paid by manager's cheque drawn on a UAE bank, handed over at the trustee office on transfer day. Plan how the funds will reach a UAE bank weeks before the transfer, not days: your own account if a bank will open one for you, or a lawyer's client account.

DLD's Digital Sale service on the Dubai Now app completes a sale online, but it is built for residents: both sides need an Emirates ID, an active UAE Pass and a UAE bank account, and the home must be in a freehold area with one owner. Non-residents use a trustee office, in person or through an attorney.

Budget the fees before you send money. On a ready home they come to about 7% of the price: the 4% transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the trustee fee, the agency fee and the NOC. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) gives the exact sum.

### Visas that property can bring

- **A two-year investor residence visa.** The Dubai Land Department's service page lists it for a sole owner of property of any value, or a joint owner whose share is worth at least AED 400,000, with an investor fee of AED 10,212.50.
- **A Golden Visa.** For property worth AED 2 million or more, in one home or several. DLD and GDRFA Dubai describe it as ten years and renewable. [The Golden Visa through property](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/golden-visa-through-property/) sets out the conditions.

In April 2026 GDRFA Dubai and DLD agreed to move property residency services into GDRFA Dubai's system. Confirm the current channel and fees before you apply, because the pages that describe them are changing.

### Tax when you own from abroad

The UAE has no income tax on individuals. Under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, income from property you hold in your own name is outside UAE corporate tax, whatever the amount, as long as the activity is not carried out, and need not be carried out, under a licence. Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT.

Your own country may tax rent and gains from Dubai property, and some countries tax worldwide income. Ask an adviser at home before you buy, not after.

### Questions

**Can a foreigner who does not live in the UAE buy property in Dubai?**
Yes. Any nationality can own freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold areas under Law No. 7 of 2006, and no residence visa is needed. A valid passport identifies a non-resident at the registration trustee.

**Can I complete a Dubai purchase without visiting?**
Yes, through an attorney holding a power of attorney. One issued abroad must be notarised there, legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate, attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, translated into Arabic and dated within the last two years.

**Do I need a UAE bank account to buy?**
Not for DLD's fees, which it accepts by ePay, Dubai Pay, Noqodi or manager's cheque. The price is paid by manager's cheque from a UAE bank by market practice, and DLD's digital sale service requires a UAE account, so most non-residents open one or use a lawyer's client account.

**Can I use DLD's online sale service from abroad?**
No. The Digital Sale service on the Dubai Now app needs an Emirates ID, an active UAE Pass and a UAE bank account from both parties, which non-residents do not have. Non-residents complete at a registration trustee office.

**Does owning property in Dubai give me a residence visa?**
It can. DLD lists a two-year investor residence visa for a sole owner of property of any value, or a joint owner with a share of at least AED 400,000, and a Golden Visa, which DLD and GDRFA Dubai describe as ten years, for property worth AED 2 million or more.

**Will I pay UAE tax on rent from a Dubai property?**
No personal income tax applies in the UAE, and rental income from property held in your own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is needed. Your country of residence may tax the income.

### Sources

- [Bayut: list of freehold areas in Dubai (August 2026)](https://www.bayut.com/mybayut/complete-list-freehold-areas-dubai/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 7 of 2006 on real property registration](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2006/Law%20No.%20(7)%20of%202006.pdf)
- [Dubai Land Department: property sale registration](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/)
- [BSA Law: Dubai's standards for powers of attorney in property deals (August 2025)](https://bsalaw.com/insight/dubais-new-standards-for-powers-of-attorney-in-property-deals/)
- [Anders: rules on powers of attorney for real estate in Dubai (November 2025)](https://anders.ae/en/services/real-estate/publication/new-rules-on-powers-of-attorney-for-real-estate-transactions-in-the-emirate-of-dubai)
- [Dubai Land Department: Digital Sale service on the Dubai Now app (October 2025)](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/news-media/dubai-land-department-unveils-digital-sale-service-on-dubai-now-app-at-gitex-global-2025)
- [Dubai Land Department: Dubai REST](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/dubai-rest/)
- [Dubai Land Department: investor visa for property owners](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-for-investor-visa/)
- [Dubai Land Department: Golden Visa for property investors](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-for-golden-visa-investor/)
- [Dubai Media Office: GDRFA Dubai and DLD residency services (April 2026)](https://mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2026/april/11-04/gdrfa)
- [Federal Tax Authority: real estate investment for natural persons (October 2024)](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2024/Real-Estate-Investment-for-natural-persons-22-10-2024.pdf)
- [UAE Government portal: taxation](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment/taxation)

## Service charges in Dubai, explained for owners and buyers

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/service-charges-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-09-16

What the annual charge pays for, who sets it, where to look it up before you buy, and what the law does when an owner stops paying.

### In short

- A service charge is the yearly amount each owner pays to manage, operate, maintain and repair the shared parts of a building or community.
- Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 stops a management company charging it until RERA has approved a budget that a certified audit firm has already approved.
- You can see the approved charge for any building on DLD's Service Charge Index, through Mollak or in the Dubai REST app.
- Unpaid charges are a lien on the home. It cannot be sold until they are cleared.

### What the charge pays for

Every apartment building and most villa communities in Dubai are jointly owned property: you own your unit, and all owners share the lobby, lifts, pool, gym, corridors, landscaping, security and the structure itself. Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 defines service charges as the annual charges collected from owners to meet the cost of managing, operating, maintaining and repairing those shared parts.

The charge is set per square foot of your unit, so a larger home pays more. Buildings with more facilities cost more to run, and so do older buildings that need more repair. A reserve fund for future replacement, such as lifts and chillers, sits inside the budget.

The charge does not cover your own unit. Repairs inside the home, your DEWA account and, where there is district cooling, your unit's chiller consumption are separate costs.

### What a budget contains

An approved budget is itemised, and the manager must show it to owners. The usual lines are:

- Cleaning, security and concierge staff
- Lifts, fire systems, pumps and air handling: maintenance contracts and repairs
- Pool, gym and landscaping
- Electricity and water for the shared areas
- Building insurance
- The management company's fee
- The reserve fund contribution for future replacement of major plant

Ask which lines rose in the last budget and why. Insurance and maintenance contracts are common reasons for an increase.

### Who sets the amount

Each jointly owned building or community has a management entity: an owners' association, the developer, or a management company. Article 27 of Law No. 6 of 2019 forbids that entity from charging owners until the Real Estate Regulatory Agency (RERA) has approved the amount. RERA will not approve a budget that a certified audit firm has not approved first.

RERA runs this through Mollak, its system for service charge budgets, invoices and the companies that manage buildings. Owners are represented by an owners committee formed under the same law, which reviews the budget and raises concerns with the manager and with RERA.

### How to check a building before you buy

1. **Look up the approved rate.** DLD's Service Charge Index lists the service charges RERA has approved for jointly owned properties. It is on the DLD website, through Mollak, and in the Dubai REST app. Search by the building or community name.
2. **Multiply by the unit's area.** The index gives a rate per square foot. Multiply by the area on the title deed to get the yearly charge for the home you are looking at.
3. **Confirm the seller is paid up.** A home cannot be disposed of while its service charges are unpaid. On a resale the developer's no-objection certificate confirms the dues are clear, and Form F records who pays the NOC fee.
4. **Ask about the reserve fund and recent increases.** A low reserve can mean a large one-off levy later. Ask the manager for the last two approved budgets.

If the seller cannot show a service charge statement, ask the manager directly before you sign Form F. The lien attaches to the unit, not to the seller: the trustee will not transfer without the NOC, and the developer will not issue it while charges are unpaid.

### Service charges and your return

The charge is an owner's cost, every year, whether the home is let or empty. Law No. 6 of 2019 defines it as a charge collected from owners, so a landlord pays it, not the tenant, unless a tenancy contract says otherwise. Take it off the rent before you judge a home's yield, and add it to your running costs alongside insurance and any management fee.

If you are comparing two homes at similar prices, the service charge can decide between them. A difference of a few dirhams per square foot on a large apartment adds up over the years you own it.

### When an owner does not pay

- The management entity holds a lien over the unit, and the unit cannot be sold until the charges are paid (Article 32)
- After a written notice approved by RERA, the owner has 30 days to pay before the entity can enforce the claim through the execution judge at the Rental Disputes Center
- The judge can order the unit sold at public auction, with the court and legal fees falling on the owner

If you believe a charge is wrong, raise it with the owners committee and through Mollak before you withhold payment. Non-payment does not pause the lien.

### If you disagree with the budget

The audit and RERA approval exist to keep budgets honest, but they do not make every budget right for every owner. The owners committee is the first route. It can ask the manager for the detail behind any line, and it can take concerns to RERA through Mollak. Disputes over jointly owned property go to the Rental Disputes Center, which has handled them since Law No. 6 of 2019.

- Ask the manager for the line-by-line budget and the audit firm's approval
- Raise it through the owners committee, which can take it to RERA through Mollak
- For a claim, file at the Rental Disputes Center

### Questions

**What are service charges in Dubai?**
The annual charges each owner pays to manage, operate, maintain and repair the shared parts of a jointly owned building or community, as defined in Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019.

**Who approves service charges in Dubai?**
RERA. Under Article 27 of Law No. 6 of 2019 a management entity may not charge owners until RERA has approved the amount, and RERA first requires a budget approved by a certified audit firm.

**How do I find the service charge for a building in Dubai?**
On the Dubai Land Department's Service Charge Index, available on the DLD website, through Mollak and in the Dubai REST app. It gives the approved rate per square foot, which you multiply by the unit's area.

**Does the tenant or the owner pay service charges?**
The owner. Law No. 6 of 2019 defines service charges as charges collected from owners. A tenancy contract can shift some costs, but the obligation to the building sits with the owner.

**Can I sell a home with unpaid service charges?**
No. Unpaid service charges are a lien on the unit under Law No. 6 of 2019, and the unit cannot be disposed of until they are paid. The developer's NOC on a resale confirms the dues are clear.

**What happens if an owner refuses to pay service charges?**
After a RERA-approved written notice and 30 days to pay, the management entity can enforce through the execution judge at the Rental Disputes Center, who may order the unit sold at auction with the costs on the owner.

**Can service charges go up?**
Yes, but only through a new budget approved by a certified audit firm and then by RERA. Ask for the last two approved budgets to see the trend before you buy.

### Sources

- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 6 of 2019 on jointly owned real property](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2019/Law%20No.%20(6)%20of%202019%20Concerning%20Ownership%20of%20Jointly%20Owned%20Real%20Property%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)
- [Dubai Land Department: Service Charge Index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index-overview/)
- [Mollak: about the system](https://mollak.dubailand.gov.ae/publicpages/about-us.html)
- [Dubai Land Department: Dubai REST](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/dubai-rest/)
- [Property Finder: no-objection certificates in Dubai (April 2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/no-objection-certificate-dubai/)
- [Rental Disputes Center: about the centre](https://rdc.gov.ae/en/about-rdc/about-rental-disputes-center/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Decree No. 26 of 2013 on the Rent Disputes Settlement Centre](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2013/Decree%2026%20of%202013.html)

## How to rent out your Dubai property

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/renting-out-property-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-09-16

The landlord's side of Dubai tenancy law: registering the contract, what rent increase the index allows, the two notice rules, holiday lets and tax.

### In short

- A tenancy contract must be registered with RERA through Ejari. Online registration costs AED 177.75.
- Rent can rise at renewal only when it is more than 10% below the rent index average for similar homes, and then by 5% to at most 20%, in bands set by Decree No. 43 of 2013.
- To change the terms or not renew, either side gives at least 90 days' notice before the contract ends, unless the contract says otherwise.
- To end a tenancy at expiry so you can sell, or move in yourself or a first-degree relative, you must give 12 months' notice through a notary public or by registered mail.
- There is no UAE income tax on individuals, and rent from property in your own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is needed.

### Register the contract on Ejari

Article 4 of Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007, as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008, requires every lease to be registered with RERA. The system is Ejari. Without it the tenant cannot connect DEWA in their name and neither side can file a case at the Rental Disputes Center. The landlord, the tenant or a holder of a power of attorney can register.

| Where you register | Fee |
| --- | --- |
| Dubai REST app or the DLD website | AED 177.75: AED 100 registration, AED 10 knowledge fee, AED 10 innovation fee, AED 55 service fee and VAT |
| A registration trustee centre | AED 100, AED 10 and AED 10, plus an AED 95 service fee and VAT |

You need the title deed, the tenant's passport and Emirates ID, your own identification and the signed contract. Register the renewal each year as well, because an expired Ejari blocks the same services as a missing one.

### How much you can raise the rent

You cannot raise the rent during a contract. At renewal, Decree No. 43 of 2013 ties any increase to how far the current rent sits below the average for similar homes in RERA's rent index:

| Current rent against the index average | Largest increase allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 10% below | None |
| 11% to 20% below | 5% |
| 21% to 30% below | 10% |
| 31% to 40% below | 15% |
| More than 40% below | 20% |

Since January 2025 the Dubai Land Department's Smart Rental Index has set that average. It classifies every building by its specification, finishes, location and facilities, so two buildings on the same street can carry different averages. The bands themselves did not change. Check the index in the Dubai REST app before you propose a new rent, because a tenant can take an increase outside the bands to the Rental Disputes Center.

### The two notice rules

- **To change the terms or not renew:** at least 90 days before the contract ends, unless the contract sets a different period (Article 14 of Law No. 26 of 2007). This covers a rent increase within the bands.
- **To end the tenancy at expiry to sell, move in, demolish and rebuild, or carry out major maintenance:** at least 12 months before the eviction date, served through a notary public or by registered mail (Article 25(2), as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008).

The moving-in ground applies when you or a first-degree relative need the home and have no other suitable property. A notice sent by email or WhatsApp does not meet the 12-month rule. If a tenant does not leave after valid notice, the Rental Disputes Center decides.

### What to put in the contract

1. **The rent and how it is paid.** The number of cheques and their dates. Fewer cheques usually suits the landlord, so ask whether it changes the rent.
2. **The security deposit.** How much, what it covers and when it is returned. A dated inventory with photographs avoids the argument at the end.
3. **Maintenance.** Who pays for what. By custom the landlord carries major items such as air conditioning and the tenant carries minor wear, but write it down.
4. **Service charges and chiller.** Service charges are the owner's cost under Law No. 6 of 2019. Say in the contract who pays any district cooling charges.
5. **Subletting and use.** Whether the tenant may sublet, and that the home is for residential use only.

Register exactly what you both signed. Extra terms go in an addendum signed by both sides, because the Rental Disputes Center reads the registered contract, not the messages around it.

### Holiday lets and shared housing

Short-term holiday lets need a holiday home permit from Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism (DET). Individual owners can register their own homes, not only companies. Gulf News lists the usual documents as the title deed or sale agreement, the developer's NOC where the building requires one, identification, a recent DEWA bill and insurance. Check DET's current requirements and fees before you list, and check your building's rules, because some owners' associations restrict short lets.

Separately, Law No. 4 of 2026, issued in March 2026, requires a permit before any unit is used as shared housing. Letting rooms to several unrelated tenants falls under it.

### Tax on the rent

- The UAE levies no income tax on individuals
- Under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, a person's income from real estate investment is outside corporate tax, whatever the amount, as long as the activity is not carried out, and need not be carried out, under a licence
- Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT; commercial property rent carries 5%

If you live outside the UAE, your own country may tax the rent. Non-resident owners should read [buying property in Dubai from abroad](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/buying-property-in-dubai-from-abroad/) and ask an adviser at home.

### Questions

**Do I have to register a tenancy on Ejari?**
Yes. Article 4 of Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 requires every lease to be registered with RERA, through Ejari. Online registration costs AED 177.75 and a registration trustee centre charges an AED 95 service fee in place of the AED 55 online fee.

**How much can I raise the rent in Dubai?**
Nothing if the rent is within 10% of the index average for similar homes. Otherwise 5% when it is 11% to 20% below, 10% at 21% to 30% below, 15% at 31% to 40% below, and 20% when it is more than 40% below, under Decree No. 43 of 2013.

**What is the Smart Rental Index?**
The Dubai Land Department's rent index since January 2025. It classifies each building by specification, finishes, location and facilities to set the average rent that Decree No. 43 of 2013 measures increases against.

**How much notice must I give to raise the rent or not renew?**
At least 90 days before the contract ends, unless the contract sets another period, under Article 14 of Law No. 26 of 2007.

**How do I get my property back to sell it or live in it?**
Serve at least 12 months' notice before the eviction date, through a notary public or by registered mail, under Article 25(2) of Law No. 26 of 2007 as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008. Moving in requires that you or a first-degree relative have no other suitable home.

**Can I let my Dubai home on Airbnb?**
Only with a holiday home permit from the Department of Economy and Tourism. Individual owners can apply, with documents such as the title deed, the developer's NOC where required, identification, a DEWA bill and insurance.

**Is rental income taxed in Dubai?**
The UAE has no personal income tax, and under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023 rent from property held in your own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is required. Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT.

### Sources

- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 26 of 2007 on landlords and tenants](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2007/Law%20No.%20(26)%20of%202007.html)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 33 of 2008 amending Law No. 26 of 2007](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2009/Law%20No.%20(33)%20of%202008%20Amending%20Law%20No.%20(26)%20of%202007.html)
- [Dubai Land Department: register or renew an Ejari contract](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Decree No. 43 of 2013 on rent increases](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2013/Decree%20No.%20(43)%20of%202013%20Determining%20Rent%20Increase%20for%20Real%20Property.html)
- [Dubai Media Office: the Smart Rental Index (January 2025)](https://mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2025/january/02-01/smart-rental)

- [Dubai Media Office: law regulating shared housing (March 2026)](https://mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2026/march/11-03/mohammed-bin-rashid-issues-law-regulating-the-management)

## Handover and snagging: taking the keys to a new Dubai home

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/handover-and-snagging-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-09-16

The completion certificate, your title deed, the inspection before you accept, and the years the developer stays responsible for defects.

### In short

- When a project receives its completion certificate, the developer must register each sold unit in the name of the buyer who has met their obligations. Your Oqood registration becomes a title deed.
- Snagging is the inspection you carry out before you accept the home. You list every defect and every piece of incomplete work for the developer to put right.
- Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 makes the developer liable for defective installations for one year from handover and for structural defects for ten years from the completion certificate.
- Any clause that cuts those liabilities short is void.

### The completion certificate and your deed

A building is complete when its planning authority says so by issuing a completion certificate. Depending on the area that authority is the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees or Dubai Municipality. Until the certificate exists the developer cannot hand over.

Once it exists, Article 8 of Law No. 13 of 2008 requires the developer to enter the project in the property register and to register each sold unit in the name of the buyer who has met their obligations. That is the moment your Oqood registration gives way to a title deed. DLD charges a fee to issue the deed; ask the developer for the amount. If you still owe an instalment, settle it first, because the registration waits for buyers who have paid.

### Before handover day

- Read the handover notice for what the developer asks you to pay: the final instalment, any administration charge, and the first service charge period
- Check the service charge against what the sale agreement said, and ask for the RERA-approved budget
- Confirm the DEWA connection process and whether a deposit is collected at handover
- Book a snagging inspection for a date before you sign the handover documents, not after

The developer's handover team will have an appointment system and a document list, usually your identification and proof that the final payment has cleared. Ask for the list in advance so the appointment is not wasted, and ask whether the keys are released on the day or after the deed is issued.

### The snagging inspection

Snagging is market practice rather than a legal step, so nothing in the law forces the developer to wait for it. The developer's handover documents usually include an acceptance form, and once you sign it, the developer can treat the home as accepted. Inspect first. Walk every room with a checklist, or hire an inspector who does this for a living, and hand the developer a written, dated list with photographs.

1. **Finishes.** Walls, ceilings, floors, tiling, joinery, doors and windows. Look for cracks, chips, gaps, scratches and uneven lines.
2. **Installations.** Air conditioning, electrics, every socket and switch, water pressure, hot water, drainage and extraction, each tested while running.
3. **Kitchen and bathrooms.** Appliances, silicone and grout, taps and shower screens, waterproofing under and around wet areas.
4. **Against the contract.** Layout, size and specification checked against the sale and purchase agreement and the brochure you bought from.
5. **Outside.** Balcony drainage, railings, external doors and, on a villa, the boundary wall, garden drainage and the roof.

Agree a date for the developer to clear the list and a second visit to confirm it. Keep copies of everything. The one-year installation liability starts at handover, so it has already started once you take the keys.

### How long the developer is liable

| Defect | Developer liable for | Counted from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defective installations: mechanical, electrical, sanitary and sewerage | 1 year | Handover of the unit, or the completion certificate if the owner refuses to take possession |
| Defects in the structural parts of the building | 10 years | The completion certificate |

Both periods come from Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019, and the same article makes any agreement to the contrary void. A clause in your sale agreement that shortens them has no effect. Separately, the UAE's Civil Transactions Law covers contractors and engineers. Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025 holds them jointly liable for ten years for collapse or for defects that threaten a building's stability or safety, in Articles 821 to 824, in force from 1 June 2026.

Report defects in writing as soon as you find them, with dates, so that a claim inside the period is easy to prove.

### Delays, defaults and cancelled projects

If the delay is yours, Law No. 13 of 2008 as amended by Law No. 19 of 2020 applies. After a 30-day notice served through DLD, the developer may terminate. It may keep up to 40% of the unit's value where the project is more than 60% complete, or up to 25% below that. It must refund the rest within a year, or within 60 days of reselling the unit, whichever comes first.

If the delay is the developer's, the sale and purchase agreement governs. Read the clause on late completion before you sign, because it sets whatever compensation you are entitled to. If a project never starts for reasons outside the developer's control, or RERA cancels it, the developer must refund buyers' payments under the escrow law.

### Selling before the keys

You can resell an off-plan home before completion. Under Article 3 of Law No. 13 of 2008 every such sale must be entered in the interim register, or it is void. The developer sets its own conditions for the resale NOC, written into the sale and purchase agreement, including how much of the price must already be paid. [Selling property in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/selling-property-in-dubai/) covers the steps.

Ask the developer for its consent conditions and any administration fee in writing before you agree a price with a buyer. No deed changes hands; the Oqood record is updated to the buyer's name, and the deed is issued to them at completion.

### Questions

**When does an off-plan buyer get the title deed?**
After the project's completion certificate is issued. Article 8 of Law No. 13 of 2008 then requires the developer to register each sold unit in the name of the buyer who has met their obligations. DLD charges a fee to issue the deed; the developer can tell you the amount.

**What is snagging?**
The inspection of a new home before you accept it. You list defects and incomplete work for the developer to put right. It is market practice, not a legal procedure, so arrange it before you sign the handover documents.

**How long must a developer fix defects in Dubai?**
One year from handover for defective mechanical, electrical, sanitary and sewerage installations, and ten years from the completion certificate for structural defects, under Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019. Any agreement to the contrary is void.

**Who issues the completion certificate?**
The planning authority for the area: the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees or Dubai Municipality.

**What happens if I stop paying before handover?**
After a 30-day notice through DLD the developer may terminate and keep up to 40% of the unit's value on a project more than 60% complete, or up to 25% below that, refunding the balance within a year or 60 days of resale, under Law No. 13 of 2008 as amended by Law No. 19 of 2020.

**What if the developer is late?**
Your sale and purchase agreement sets your entitlement, so read the late completion clause before you sign. If the project never starts or RERA cancels it, the escrow law requires your payments to be refunded.

**Can I sell an off-plan home before handover?**
Yes, subject to the developer's conditions and NOC. Under Article 3 of Law No. 13 of 2008 the sale must be entered in DLD's interim register or it is void.

### Sources

- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 6 of 2019 on jointly owned real property](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2019/Law%20No.%20(6)%20of%202019%20Concerning%20Ownership%20of%20Jointly%20Owned%20Real%20Property%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 13 of 2008 on the interim property register](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2008/Law%20No.%20(13)%20of%202008.html)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 19 of 2020 amending Law No. 13 of 2008](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2020/Law%20No.%20(19)%20of%202020%20Amending%20Law%20No.%20(13)%20of%202008%20Regulating%20the%20Interim%20Real%20Property%20Register%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 8 of 2007 on escrow accounts](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2007/Law%20No.%20(8)%20of%202007.html)
- [Charles Russell Speechlys: decennial liability under the new UAE Civil Code (May 2026)](https://www.charlesrussellspeechlys.com/en/insights/expert-insights/construction-engineering-and-projects/2026/decennial-liability-and-subcontractors-under-the-new-uae-civil-code-articles-821-to-824/)
- [Dubai Development Authority: building completion certificate](https://dda.gov.ae/en/planning-development/construction/inspections-completions/building-completion-certificate)
- [Dubai Land Department: property sale registration](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/)

## How to sell property in Dubai, step by step

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/selling-property-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-10-17

From the listing agreement to the transfer at the trustee office: the forms you sign, the certificates you need, the fees by custom, and how an off-plan unit is sold before handover.

### In short

- A sale in Dubai runs through three RERA forms: Form A appoints your broker, Form F is the sale contract with the buyer, and the broker's Form B binds the buyer to them.
- Before transfer you need the developer's no-objection certificate, which confirms you owe the developer nothing.
- Ownership passes at a Dubai Land Department registration trustee office. By custom the buyer pays the 4% transfer fee and the agency fee is 2% plus VAT.
- An off-plan unit can be sold before handover with the developer's consent. The sale is recorded on the Oqood register, not by a title deed.

### Appoint a broker with Form A

Dubai's brokers work on standard RERA contracts. Form A is the agreement between you and the brokerage to market your home. The Dubai Land Department's brokerage practice guide describes it as the marketing agreement between the seller and the brokerage, and every licensed broker must use it. If the home is jointly owned, every owner signs.

Once signed, it is submitted through DLD's Trakheesi system, which issues the advertising permit for your home. Bayut's guide notes that an owner can hold up to three Form A agreements at a time, one per brokerage, so you can give the listing to more than one firm or keep it exclusive.

- Check the broker's card and the brokerage's registration before you sign; [choosing a real estate broker in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/choosing-a-real-estate-broker-in-dubai/) shows how
- Agree the asking price, the commission and the term of the agreement in the form, not by message
- Ask how the home will be advertised: every advert must carry the Trakheesi permit number, and printed and video adverts a Madmoun QR code

### Agree the sale with Form F

When a buyer's offer is accepted, both of you sign Form F, the sale contract RERA calls the memorandum of understanding. It records the price, the deposit, the transfer date, the fees and who pays each, and the commission due to each side's broker. It is valid only once the seller and the buyer have both signed and the broker has witnessed and dated it.

By custom the buyer pays a 10% deposit on signing. The broker usually holds the deposit cheque until transfer. Form F also sets the consequences if either side withdraws, so read that clause as carefully as the price.

### Get the developer's NOC

On a resale in a freehold area the trustee will not transfer without the developer's no-objection certificate. The NOC confirms you owe the developer nothing: no service charges, no penalties, no restriction on the unit. You apply for it, and the developer issues it electronically through the Dubai REST app.

Developers charge AED 500 to 5,000 for the NOC, and each sets its own fee and processing time. Form F records which side pays it. Clear any service charge arrears before you apply, because the developer will not issue the certificate while they stand. Under Law No. 6 of 2019 a home cannot be sold while its service charges are unpaid; [service charges in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/service-charges-in-dubai/) explains the lien.

### The transfer at the trustee office

Ownership passes at a Dubai Land Department registration trustee office. Both sides attend, or send an attorney with a valid power of attorney. You bring the original title deed, the NOC, Form F and your identification: an Emirates ID, or a passport for a non-resident. The buyer brings manager's cheques for the price and the fees. The trustee registers the sale, DLD issues the new deed in the buyer's name, and you leave with the cheque.

| Fee | Amount | Paid by custom |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DLD transfer fee | 4% of the price. DLD's schedule splits it 2% and 2%, but Form F usually puts it on the buyer | Buyer |
| Title deed fees | AED 520 for an apartment or villa | Buyer |
| Registration trustee fee | AED 4,000 plus VAT at AED 500,000 and above; AED 2,000 plus VAT below | Buyer |
| Agency fee | 2% of the price plus VAT, the customary rate; it is set by agreement, not by law | Buyer, unless Form A or Form F says otherwise |
| Developer NOC | AED 500 to 5,000, set by the developer | As agreed in Form F |

Property Finder's guide confirms the 2% resale commission is usually paid by the buyer, and that an exclusive agreement can change who pays. If your Form A promises the brokerage a fee from you, that fee is due at transfer. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) shows the buyer's side at any price.

### How long it takes

Nothing in the law sets the timetable. A sale with the developer's NOC in hand can complete soon after Form F. Set the completion date in Form F with that step in mind, and ask for the NOC early.

1. **Form A signed, advert permitted.** The brokerage markets the home under its Trakheesi permit.
2. **Offer accepted, Form F signed.** The buyer pays the customary 10% deposit.
3. **NOC requested.** You apply to the developer; arrears must be cleared first.
4. **Transfer.** Both sides at the trustee office with the deed, the NOC, Form F and the cheques.

### Selling an off-plan unit before handover

An off-plan unit has no title deed yet. What you own is your contract with the developer, registered on DLD's Oqood interim register. Selling it means assigning that contract to a new buyer, who takes over the remaining instalments. Under Article 3 of Law No. 13 of 2008 the sale must be entered in the interim register, or it is void.

- The developer must consent and issue an NOC, and most sale agreements allow a resale only once a share of the price has been paid; Betterhomes puts the usual threshold at 30% to 40%, but your own agreement sets the figure
- Your instalments must be up to date, because a developer will not consent while arrears stand
- The buyer pays the 4% DLD fee on the resale price, and the developer may charge its own transfer or administration fee, so ask for the amounts in writing
- The new buyer's name replaces yours on Oqood, and the title deed is issued to them at completion

[Handover and snagging in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/handover-and-snagging-in-dubai/) explains what happens if you keep the unit to completion.

### Questions

**What is Form A in Dubai real estate?**
The RERA listing agreement between a seller and a brokerage. It authorises the brokerage to market the home and, once submitted through Trakheesi, produces the advertising permit. An owner can hold up to three at a time, one per brokerage.

**What is Form F?**
The RERA sale contract between buyer and seller, often called the MOU. It records the price, deposit, transfer date, fees and commissions, and it is valid once both parties have signed and the broker has witnessed and dated it.

**Who pays the 4% DLD transfer fee, the buyer or the seller?**
By custom the buyer. DLD's own schedule divides the 4% equally between buyer and seller, so the split is a matter for Form F, and the market practice is to put the whole fee on the buyer.

**Does the seller pay a commission in Dubai?**
Usually not on a residential resale. The customary 2% plus VAT is paid by the buyer, though an exclusive listing agreement can put a fee on the seller. The rate is set by agreement, not by law.

**What is a developer NOC and do I need one to sell?**
A no-objection certificate from the developer confirming you owe nothing on the unit. The trustee requires it on a resale in a freehold area. Developers charge AED 500 to 5,000, and Form F records who pays.

**Can I sell an off-plan property before handover in Dubai?**
Yes, with the developer's consent. The contract is assigned to the new buyer and the change is registered on DLD's Oqood interim register. Most developers require a share of the price to have been paid first; the sale agreement sets it.

**How long does it take to sell a property in Dubai?**
The law sets no period. A sale with the developer's NOC in hand completes soon after Form F, so ask the developer for the NOC early.

### Sources

- [Dubai Land Department: Real Estate Brokerage Practice Guide, second edition (November 2024)](https://dubailand.gov.ae/media/i31iv1n0/real_estate_brokerage_practice_guide_2024.pdf)
- [Bayut: RERA forms for buyers and sellers in Dubai (October 2026)](https://www.bayut.com/mybayut/guide-rera-forms-dubai/)
- [Bayut: Trakheesi advertising permits (August 2026)](https://www.bayut.com/mybayut/trakheesi/)
- [Property Finder: Trakheesi permits (January 2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/trakheesi/)
- [Dubai Land Department: Madmoun QR codes on property adverts (April 2023)](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/news-media/dubai-land-department-provides-madmoun-service-to-verify-validity-of-real-estate-ads-via-qr-codes/)
- [Meraas: guide to Form F (April 2026)](https://meraas.com/en/latest-post/journal/complete-guide-form-f-dubai)
- [Property Finder: no-objection certificates in Dubai (April 2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/no-objection-certificate-dubai/)
- [Dubai Land Department: Dubai REST](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/dubai-rest/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 6 of 2019 on jointly owned real property](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2019/Law%20No.%20(6)%20of%202019%20Concerning%20Ownership%20of%20Jointly%20Owned%20Real%20Property%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)
- [Dubai Land Department: property sale registration](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/)
- [Property Finder: real estate commission in Dubai (April 2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/how-much-is-real-estate-commission-dubai/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 13 of 2008 on the interim property register](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2008/Law%20No.%20(13)%20of%202008.html)
- [Betterhomes: exiting an off-plan deal before completion (March 2026)](https://www.bhomes.com/en/blog/betterinformed/can-you-exit-an-off-plan-deal-before-completion-a-legal-overview)
