## Renting a home in Dubai: what every tenant should know

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/renting-a-home-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-10-17

The law behind a Dubai tenancy, what you pay up front, how much the rent can rise, the notice you are entitled to, and where to go when something goes wrong.

### In short

- Dubai tenancies are governed by Law No. 26 of 2007, as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008. Every contract must be registered with RERA through Ejari.
- By market custom the security deposit is 5% of the annual rent for an unfurnished home and 10% for a furnished one, and the tenant pays an agency fee of about 5% of the annual rent plus VAT.
- Rent can rise at renewal only within the bands of Decree No. 43 of 2013, measured against the Smart Rental Index, and only with 90 days' notice.
- A landlord who wants the home back at expiry to sell it or live in it must give 12 months' notice through a notary public or by registered mail. Disputes go to the Rental Disputes Center.

### The law that protects you

Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007, amended by Law No. 33 of 2008, governs the relationship between landlords and tenants. It fixes the notice periods, the grounds on which a landlord can take a home back, and the rule that a contract runs to its end date even if the home is sold. Decree No. 43 of 2013 limits rent increases. The Rental Disputes Center, set up by Decree No. 26 of 2013, decides disputes.

The centre's jurisdiction covers rent disputes across Dubai, including the free zones, except where a free zone has its own tribunal.

### What you pay to move in

| Cost | Amount | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Security deposit | 5% of the annual rent unfurnished, 10% furnished, refundable at the end | Market custom |
| Agency fee | About 5% of the annual rent plus VAT, often with a minimum the agency sets | Market custom |
| Ejari registration | AED 177.75 online through Dubai REST or the DLD website | Dubai Land Department |
| DEWA deposit | AED 2,000 for an apartment, AED 4,000 for a villa, refundable | DEWA |
| Housing fee | 5% of the annual rent, collected monthly on the DEWA bill | Dubai Municipality |

The deposit and the agency fee are custom, not law. Bayut's guide to the costs of renting gives the deposit as 5% unfurnished and 10% furnished, and the agency fee as 5% or more of the annual rent. Property Finder's guide puts the residential agency fee at about 5%, often with a minimum of around AED 5,000, paid by the tenant with VAT added. Both can be negotiated, and the agency fee must be declared in the contract.

The landlord may deduct from the deposit for damage beyond ordinary wear, which in practice means repainting and minor repairs. Photograph the home on the day you move in and send the pictures to the agent.

### Rent cheques

Rent in Dubai is usually paid by cheque, in a number of instalments agreed in the contract. One cheque for the year is the landlord's preference and often earns a lower rent; two or four cheques are common. The cheques are post-dated to the instalment dates and handed over when the contract is signed. Keep the account funded on each date.

Keep a copy of every cheque and a receipt for every payment, naming the property and the period.

### Register the contract on Ejari

Article 4 of Law No. 26 of 2007 requires every lease to be registered with RERA. The system is Ejari, and either side can register, though the tenant usually pays. Registration online through the Dubai REST app or the DLD website costs AED 177.75: AED 100 registration, AED 10 knowledge fee, AED 10 innovation fee, AED 55 service fee and VAT. A registration trustee centre charges an AED 95 service fee instead of AED 55.

You need the signed contract, your passport, visa and Emirates ID, and the landlord's title deed and identification. The Ejari certificate is what DEWA asks for to connect water and electricity, what your employer or school may ask for as proof of address, and what the Rental Disputes Center requires before it hears a case. Renew it with each renewal of the contract.

### Connecting DEWA

Dubai Electricity and Water Authority connects the home in your name once Ejari is registered. Bayut lists the refundable deposit as AED 2,000 for an apartment and AED 4,000 for a villa, with a connection charge of AED 100 for small meters and AED 300 for large ones plus small knowledge and innovation fees. The 5% housing fee is a Dubai Municipality charge on tenants, spread across the year on the DEWA bill. In buildings with district cooling, the chiller account is separate, and the contract should say who pays it.

- Apply once Ejari is registered, with the certificate, your Emirates ID and the deposit
- Close the account when you move out; the deposit is refunded after the final bill

### How much the rent can rise

Not during the contract. At renewal, Decree No. 43 of 2013 allows an increase only when the current rent sits more than 10% below the average for similar homes in RERA's index, and caps it in bands:

| Your rent against the index average | Largest increase allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 10% below | None |
| 11% to 20% below | 5% |
| 21% to 30% below | 10% |
| 31% to 40% below | 15% |
| More than 40% below | 20% |

Since January 2025 the average comes from the Dubai Land Department's Smart Rental Index, which rates each building on its specification, finishes, location and facilities. You can check the index in the Dubai REST app. A landlord who wants an increase must tell you at least 90 days before the contract ends, under Article 14 of Law No. 26 of 2007, unless the contract sets a different period. An increase outside the bands, or one notified late, can be challenged at the Rental Disputes Center.

### When a landlord can ask you to leave

During the contract, only on the grounds in Article 25(1) of Law No. 26 of 2007, which include not paying rent within 30 days of a written notice, subletting without the landlord's written consent, using the home for an illegal purpose or causing it damage. A sale of the building is not a ground: the new owner takes over the contract.

At the end of the contract, only on the grounds in Article 25(2), as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008: the owner wants to sell, the owner or a first-degree relative needs the home and has no other suitable property, the building is to be demolished and rebuilt, or it needs major maintenance that cannot be done with you in it. In every case the landlord must give at least 12 months' notice before the eviction date, through a notary public or by registered mail. A message or an email does not count.

If you want to leave or change the terms yourself, you give the same 90 days' notice before expiry. Leaving early is governed by the contract, which usually sets a penalty, so read that clause before you sign.

### The Rental Disputes Center

The Rental Disputes Center is a judicial body within the Dubai Land Department, established by Decree No. 26 of 2013. It has exclusive jurisdiction over rent disputes between landlords and tenants in Dubai, including the free zones that have no tribunal of their own. Since 2019 it also hears disputes over jointly owned property under Law No. 6 of 2019.

- A case starts in the conciliation department, which tries to settle it within 15 days of the parties' first appearance; a settlement it approves can be enforced like a judgment
- If conciliation fails, a first instance committee decides, and an appeal committee hears appeals where the decree allows one
- The judgment execution department enforces decisions, including eviction orders and money claims
- Cases can be filed and followed through the Dubai REST app; a registration fee applies, and half of it is refunded if the case settles in conciliation

Typical tenant cases are an increase outside the bands, a deposit not returned, an eviction notice served without 12 months or without a notary, and repairs the landlord will not do. Bring the Ejari certificate, the contract, the cheques and every message.

### Questions

**What law covers tenants in Dubai?**
Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007, as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008, with rent increases limited by Decree No. 43 of 2013. Disputes are decided by the Rental Disputes Center, set up by Decree No. 26 of 2013.

**How much is the security deposit for renting in Dubai?**
By market custom 5% of the annual rent for an unfurnished home and 10% for a furnished one. It is refundable at the end, less any deduction for damage beyond ordinary wear. The figure is custom, not a legal cap.

**How much is the agency fee for a tenant in Dubai?**
By market custom about 5% of the annual rent plus VAT, often with a minimum the agency sets. It is negotiable and must be declared in the contract.

**Is Ejari compulsory for tenants?**
Yes. Article 4 of Law No. 26 of 2007 requires every lease to be registered with RERA through Ejari. Online registration costs AED 177.75, and DEWA, employers and the Rental Disputes Center all ask for the certificate.

**How much can my landlord raise the rent?**
Nothing if your rent is within 10% of the Smart Rental Index average for similar homes. Otherwise 5%, 10%, 15% or at most 20% depending on how far below the average it sits, under Decree No. 43 of 2013, and only with 90 days' notice before the contract ends.

**Can my landlord evict me to sell the property?**
Only at the end of the contract and only with at least 12 months' notice served through a notary public or by registered mail, under Article 25(2) of Law No. 26 of 2007 as amended. Until then the contract stands, and a buyer takes it over.

**What does the Rental Disputes Center do?**
It decides disputes between landlords and tenants in Dubai. A case goes first to conciliation, then to a first instance committee, with an appeal committee and an enforcement department. Cases can be filed through the Dubai REST app.

**Who pays the DEWA deposit and housing fee?**
The tenant. Bayut lists the refundable DEWA deposit as AED 2,000 for an apartment and AED 4,000 for a villa, and the Dubai Municipality housing fee as 5% of the annual rent, collected monthly on the DEWA bill.

### Sources

- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 33 of 2008 amending Law No. 26 of 2007](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2009/Law%20No.%20(33)%20of%202008%20Amending%20Law%20No.%20(26)%20of%202007.html)
- [Dubai Land Department: register or renew an Ejari contract](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Decree No. 43 of 2013 on rent increases](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2013/Decree%20No.%20(43)%20of%202013%20Determining%20Rent%20Increase%20for%20Real%20Property.html)
- [Dubai Media Office: the Smart Rental Index (January 2025)](https://mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2025/january/02-01/smart-rental)
- [Bayut: the costs of renting in Dubai (October 2026)](https://www.bayut.com/mybayut/hidden-costs-renting-dubai/)

- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Decree No. 26 of 2013 on the Rent Disputes Settlement Centre](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2013/Decree%2026%20of%202013.html)
- [Dubai Land Department: Dubai REST](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/dubai-rest/)
- [Dubai Legislation Portal: Law No. 6 of 2019 on jointly owned real property](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2019/Law%20No.%20(6)%20of%202019%20Concerning%20Ownership%20of%20Jointly%20Owned%20Real%20Property%20in%20the%20Emirate%20of%20Dubai.html)

## Investing in Dubai property: how to judge a deal

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/investing-in-dubai-property/
Updated: 2026-10-17

A method, not a forecast: work out the yield that is left after costs, read the price data, weigh off-plan against ready, and understand the tax and visa rules that apply.

### In short

- Gross yield is the annual rent divided by the price. Net yield takes off service charges, management, vacancy and the buying costs before it divides, and it is the number that matters.
- The UAE levies no income tax on individuals, and rent from property held in your own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is required.
- A ready home earns from the day of transfer. An off-plan home earns nothing until handover, but its payments are spread over the build.
- Property worth AED 2 million or more can support a Golden Visa application.

### Gross yield and net yield

Gross yield is the simplest measure and the one adverts use. Divide the annual rent by the purchase price and multiply by 100. It ignores every cost.

Net yield is the measure to decide on. Start with the annual rent. Take off the service charge, the management fee if an agent runs the tenancy, an allowance for the weeks the home may sit empty between tenants, insurance and maintenance. Divide what is left by the full cost of buying: the price plus the DLD transfer and title deed fees, the trustee fee, the agency fee and the NOC. Multiply by 100.

| Measure | Formula |
| --- | --- |
| Gross yield | Annual rent ÷ purchase price × 100 |
| Net yield | (Annual rent − service charge − management − vacancy allowance − insurance and maintenance) ÷ (price + buying costs) × 100 |

Rent and price change by building and by month, so we publish no yield figures. Use the formula with the actual asking rent for the unit, the RERA-approved service charge for the building, and the fees from the [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/).

### The costs that reduce the yield

- **Buying costs.** On a ready home about 7% of the price: the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the trustee fee of AED 4,000 plus VAT at AED 500,000 and above, the customary 2% agency fee plus VAT, and a developer NOC of AED 500 to 5,000. On an off-plan home, 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20.
- **Service charges.** An annual owner's cost approved by RERA under Law No. 6 of 2019. Look the building up on DLD's Service Charge Index before you offer; [service charges in Dubai](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/service-charges-in-dubai/) explains how.
- **Management.** If an agent finds tenants and runs the tenancy, their fee is set by agreement. Ask for it as a percentage of rent and as a fixed sum, and check what it covers.
- **Vacancy.** Every change of tenant costs weeks of rent plus repainting. Build an allowance in rather than assuming twelve months of rent every year.
- **Ejari and letting fees.** Ejari registration is AED 177.75 online. The tenant's agency fee is by custom paid by the tenant, not the landlord.

A lower service charge or a shorter vacancy can outweigh a higher gross yield.

### Tax on a Dubai investment

The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals, so rent received by a person is not taxed as income. Under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023, as explained by the Federal Tax Authority, a natural person's income from real estate investment is outside corporate tax, whatever the amount, as long as the activity is not carried out, and is not required to be carried out, under a licence. The FTA's guidance covers income from selling as well as letting such property.

VAT does apply to property, but residential leases are generally exempt and the first supply of a new residential home within three years of completion is zero-rated. Commercial property carries 5%. Your own country may tax the rent and any gain, so take advice there before you buy.

### Short lets and holiday homes

A home can be let by the night, but only with a holiday home permit from the Department of Economy and Tourism, and individual owners can apply. Gulf News lists the usual documents as the title deed or sale agreement, the developer's NOC where the building requires one, identification, a recent DEWA bill and insurance. Short lets bring higher gross income and higher costs: furnishing, cleaning, utilities and platform fees. Run the net yield formula on both models before you choose, and check that the building allows short lets.

Separately, Law No. 4 of 2026 requires a permit before a unit is used as shared housing, so letting rooms to several tenants is not a way round the rules.

### Reading the price data

The Dubai Land Department publishes every registered transaction as an open dataset on Data.Dubai. Our [Dubai property prices](https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-prices/) pages are built from it. They show, for Dubai and for seven of its main communities, the number of sales, the median price and the median price per square foot by quarter, the change over the last twelve months and the share of sales that were off-plan. The analysis is ours, not DLD's.

1. **Compare the asking price with the median price per square foot.** A price well above the median needs a reason: floor, view, condition or size.
2. **Look at the trend, not one quarter.** Twelve months tells you more than three, because launches and seasons move the quarterly figures.
3. **Read the off-plan share.** A high share means the area's future supply is still under construction, which matters for rent when it all hands over.
4. **Check the rent side separately.** The Smart Rental Index in the Dubai REST app shows what similar homes rent for, and it is the index the law uses to cap increases.

### Off-plan or ready for an investor

A ready home earns rent from the day of transfer. An off-plan home earns nothing until handover. In exchange the payments are spread over the build and the money sits in the project's escrow account under Law No. 8 of 2007.

If you buy off-plan to let, treat the first service charge, the handover date and the rent at handover as unknowns. [Off-plan or ready](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/off-plan-vs-ready-property-in-dubai/) compares the two in full.

### The risks to price in

- Rent on a sitting tenant can rise only within the bands of Decree No. 43 of 2013, so a home let below the index catches up slowly
- Service charges are approved yearly and can rise with a new budget
- Vacancy runs longer in areas with a lot of new supply handing over at once
- An off-plan handover can slip, and the sale agreement sets what you get if it does
- Prices move in both directions; the DLD data shows the last twelve months, not the next

These are the inputs the net yield formula needs, and the ones an advert leaves out.

### The Golden Visa link

Property worth AED 2 million or more lets the owner apply for a Golden Visa, which the Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai describe as ten years and renewable.

- The AED 2 million can be in one home or several
- A jointly owned home counts only when your own share is worth AED 2 million or more
- The federal government portal shows a different term from DLD and GDRFA, and the official pages do not address off-plan property

[The Golden Visa through property](https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/golden-visa-through-property/) sets out the conditions and what the official pages leave open.

### Questions

**How do I calculate rental yield on a Dubai property?**
Gross yield is the annual rent divided by the price, times 100. Net yield takes off service charges, management, a vacancy allowance, insurance and maintenance, then divides by the price plus buying costs. Net yield is the figure to decide on.

**What costs reduce the return on a Dubai investment property?**
Buying costs of about 7% on a ready home, the annual service charge, any management fee, vacancy between tenants and maintenance.

**Is rental income taxed in Dubai?**
Not for individuals. The UAE has no personal income tax, and under Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023 a person's income from property held in their own name is outside corporate tax when no licence is required. Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT.

**Is there capital gains tax on property in Dubai?**
The UAE levies no income tax on individuals. The Federal Tax Authority's guidance on real estate investment by natural persons covers income from selling as well as letting property held in their own name, and treats it as outside corporate tax when no licence is required.

**Can I let my investment property as a holiday home?**
Yes, with a holiday home permit from the Department of Economy and Tourism, which individual owners can apply for. Check the building's rules as well, and compare the net yield of short and long lets before choosing.

**Where can I see Dubai property prices by area?**
On our Dubai property prices pages, built from the Dubai Land Department's open transactions dataset on Data.Dubai. They show sales counts, median prices and price per square foot by quarter for Dubai and for seven of its main communities.

**Is off-plan or ready better for investment in Dubai?**
A ready home earns rent at once. An off-plan home earns nothing until handover, but spreads the payments and holds them in escrow. The choice depends on when you need the income.

**Does a Dubai investment property qualify me for a Golden Visa?**
Property worth AED 2 million or more does, in one home or several. The Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai describe the visa as ten years and renewable.

- [Dubai Land Department: Service Charge Index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index-overview/)
- [Dubai Land Department: register or renew an Ejari contract](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/)

- [Dubai Land Department: Golden Visa for property investors](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/request-for-golden-visa-investor/)
- [GDRFA Dubai: Golden Visa for property investors](https://www.gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/8ea80da4-f43e-11eb-0320-0050569629e8)

## How to choose a real estate broker in Dubai

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/guides/choosing-a-real-estate-broker-in-dubai/
Updated: 2026-10-17

The checks to run before you sign, the forms a licensed broker must use, what commission is by custom, the 2026 ban on cold contact, and the questions worth asking before you sign.

### In short

- Every broker in Dubai must hold a RERA broker card with a broker registration number (BRN), and work for a brokerage with an office registration number (ORN). Both can be checked in the Dubai REST app.
- A genuine advert carries a Trakheesi permit number, the broker's and office's registration numbers and, on printed and video adverts, a Madmoun QR code.
- Licensed brokers work on RERA's standard contracts: Form A with the seller, Form B with the buyer, Form F between buyer and seller.
- Since February 2026 a DLD circular bars brokerages from contacting owners or investors to offer, market or buy property; brokers may contact only owners who have registered on RERA's green list. In 2022 RERA set the penalty for cold calling at an AED 50,000 fine, a card suspension of at least three months, or both.

### Check the broker card and BRN

Regulation No. 85 of 2006 regulates the register of real estate brokers in Dubai. A person may not act as a broker without being on it. The Dubai Land Department's brokerage practice guide sets out the route: the brokerage obtains a licence, registers it on DLD's Trakheesi system, and applies there for each broker's card, which is issued electronically once the fees are paid.

Ask the broker for the card. It names the broker and the brokerage and carries the broker registration number (BRN). Then check it yourself. The Dubai REST app, which RERA requires every broker to use, holds the register of brokers and their performance levels. Search by name or BRN and confirm the card is active, the photograph matches and the brokerage named is the one you are dealing with.

### Check the brokerage and ORN

The brokerage holds its own registration, the office registration number (ORN), issued through Trakheesi with its registration certificate. Both the BRN and the ORN must appear on the firm's adverts. A valid broker card does not help if the office behind it is suspended, so check the firm as well as the person, in the same app. RERA also classifies brokerages and brokers, and the guide says every broker should aim for a five-star rating or the golden category; the rating shows in the app.

- Search the brokerage by name or ORN and confirm it is active
- Confirm the broker's card names this brokerage
- Check the expiry dates on both

### Check the advert

- **Trakheesi permit number.** The brokerage must obtain a permit for every advert through Trakheesi and show the number on it. The permit is tied to a Form A signed by the owner, so a permit means the owner has agreed to have the home marketed.
- **Madmoun QR code.** Printed and video adverts must carry a QR code, mandatory since 24 April 2023, which opens the permit details so you can confirm the advert is genuine.
- **ORN and BRN.** Both registration numbers must appear on the advert.
- **Off-plan adverts.** These must also show the developer, the project's escrow account number and the expected completion date, and the broker must hold a marketing agreement with the developer. You can check that a project is registered in the Dubai REST app's Mashrooi section.

An advert without a permit number is either unlicensed or an invitation to contact someone who is not the listing broker. Either way, do not deal with it.

### The forms a licensed broker uses

RERA requires brokers to use its smart contracts. The brokerage practice guide names three:

| Form | Between | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Form A | Seller and brokerage | Appoints the brokerage to market the home; submitted through Trakheesi to obtain the advertising permit |
| Form B | Buyer and broker | Records what you want to buy, your budget, the commission and how the agreement ends |
| Form F | Seller and buyer | The sale contract, witnessed and dated by the broker, recording price, deposit, fees and each side's commission |

A broker who asks you to sign something else, or nothing at all, is working outside the system. Bayut's guide adds that a buyer who wants to end a Form B for cause does so in writing, with the reason and the date. A dispute over Form F can be taken to RERA's amicable settlement service through Trakheesi before it goes to court.

### What commission is by custom

No law fixes the rate. Property Finder's guide gives the customary figures: on a residential resale about 2% of the price plus VAT, usually paid by the buyer, with lower rates sometimes negotiated on high-value homes; on a rental about 5% of the annual rent plus VAT, paid by the tenant, often with a minimum the agency sets. On an off-plan sale from a developer the developer usually pays the broker, so the buyer pays no brokerage fee.

Only a licensed brokerage may charge commission, and the amount must be written into Form B and Form F. If a broker quotes a rate, ask whether it includes VAT, and have the figure in the form before you pay anything. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) shows the customary 2% alongside the other fees.

### The ban on cold contact

The brokerage practice guide describes RERA's green list: owners who register on it agree to be contacted by brokers, and brokers may not contact owners who have not. On 27 February 2026 DLD issued a circular on communication with property owners and the prohibition of cold calling. It is listed on DLD's rules and regulations page. It bars brokerages from obtaining owner or investor data by unlawful means and from contacting owners or investors by phone or any other channel to offer, market or buy property.

RERA's stated penalty for cold calling, set out when it fined a brokerage in April 2022, is AED 50,000 and/or suspension of the broker's card for no less than three months. That case suspended nine brokers. If a broker calls you about a home you never listed, you can report it through the Report Malicious Calls service in the Dubai REST app. 

### What a good broker does

- Shows you the card before you ask, and names the brokerage on it
- Puts the listing agreement, the buyer agreement and the sale contract on the RERA forms, with the commission written in
- Tells you the fees in full before you offer, including the ones that are custom rather than law
- Says what they do not know, and checks rather than guesses: the service charge and the NOC fee
- Checks a project's registration and escrow account before marketing it off-plan
- Keeps the deposit cheque safe and hands it over only on the terms in Form F

None of this is extra service. It is what the licence requires.

### Questions to ask before you sign

1. **What is your BRN and the brokerage's ORN?** Then check both in the Dubai REST app while they wait.
2. **Is this listing under a Form A, and does the advert have a permit?** If not, the owner may not have agreed to sell through this broker.
3. **What is your commission, with VAT, and who pays it?** Have it written into Form B or Form F.
4. **What is the service charge on this building, and who pays the NOC?** The Service Charge Index gives the first; Form F settles the second.
5. **For off-plan: is the project registered, and what is the escrow account number?** Both are on the Dubai REST app and the advert.
6. **How did you get my number?** The answer should be that you gave it to them.

A licensed broker can answer all six on the spot.

### Questions

**How do I check if a real estate broker in Dubai is licensed?**
Ask for their RERA broker card and search the broker registration number (BRN) in the Dubai REST app. Confirm the card is active, the photograph matches and the brokerage named is the firm you are dealing with. Check the brokerage's office registration number (ORN) the same way.

**What is a BRN and an ORN?**
The BRN is the broker registration number on an individual broker's RERA card. The ORN is the office registration number of the brokerage. Both are issued through DLD's Trakheesi system and both must appear on adverts.

**What should a property advert in Dubai show?**
A Trakheesi permit number, the brokerage's ORN and the broker's BRN, and on printed and video adverts a Madmoun QR code, mandatory since 24 April 2023. Off-plan adverts must also show the developer, the escrow account number and the expected completion date.

**What are Forms A, B and F?**
RERA's standard contracts. Form A appoints a brokerage to market a seller's home and leads to the advertising permit. Form B is the agreement between a buyer and their broker. Form F is the sale contract between seller and buyer, witnessed by the broker.

**How much commission does a broker charge in Dubai?**
By custom about 2% of the price plus VAT on a residential resale, usually paid by the buyer, and about 5% of the annual rent plus VAT on a rental, paid by the tenant. No law fixes the rate, and it must be written into the RERA forms.

**Are brokers allowed to cold call property owners in Dubai?**
No. A DLD circular of 27 February 2026 bars brokerages from contacting owners or investors by phone or other channels to offer, market or buy property, and from obtaining their data unlawfully. Brokers may contact only owners who have registered on RERA's green list.

**What is the penalty for cold calling by a broker?**
RERA's stated penalty is a fine of AED 50,000 and/or suspension of the broker's card for at least three months. In April 2022 it fined a brokerage AED 50,000 and suspended nine of its brokers for three months. Unsolicited calls can be reported through the Dubai REST app.

**Do I need a broker to buy property in Dubai?**
No law requires one, but a licensed broker handles the RERA forms, the Trakheesi permit, the NOC and the trustee appointment, and only a licensed brokerage may charge commission. If you use one, check the card and the office first.

### Sources

- [Dubai Land Department: Real Estate Brokerage Practice Guide, second edition (November 2024)](https://dubailand.gov.ae/media/i31iv1n0/real_estate_brokerage_practice_guide_2024.pdf)

- [Property Finder: Trakheesi permits (January 2026)](https://www.propertyfinder.ae/blog/trakheesi/)

## Dubai property buying facts

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-facts/
Checked: 2026-09-16

### Buying fees

| Fee | Amount | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transfer fee, ready homes | 4% of the price, customarily paid by the buyer | Dubai Land Department |
| Title deed fees | AED 520 for an apartment or villa: AED 250 + AED 250 + AED 10 + AED 10 | Dubai Land Department |
| Registration trustee fee | AED 4,000 + VAT at AED 500,000 and above; AED 2,000 + VAT below | Dubai Land Department |
| Oqood registration, off-plan homes | 4% of the price + AED 20 | Dubai Land Department |
| Agency fee | Usually 2% of the price + VAT | Market custom |
| Developer NOC, resales | AED 500 to 5,000 | The developer |

VAT in the UAE is 5%. A ready home typically carries fees of about 7% of the price; the [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works out the exact figure.

### Who can own

Buyers of any nationality can own freehold property in Dubai's designated freehold areas, first listed in Regulation No. 3 of 2006 and extended since. A UAE residence visa is not needed to buy.

- Under Dubai Law No. 7 of 2006, non-UAE nationals may hold freehold without a time limit, or leasehold rights of up to 99 years, in designated areas
- Non-resident foreigners identify themselves with a valid passport at the registration trustee
- A power of attorney issued abroad must be notarised, legalised by the UAE embassy or consulate, attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, translated into Arabic and issued within two years (DLD Circular No. 29/R/2025, as summarised by Dubai law firms)

### Off-plan protections

- Under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007, off-plan payments go into an escrow account for the project and may be used only to build it
- The developer's creditors cannot seize money held in a project escrow account
- Off-plan sales are registered on the Dubai Land Department's Oqood system before a title deed exists
- Since April 2024, each off-plan unit needs its own advertising permit, not only the project

### Advertising rules

- Every property advert in Dubai must show its Trakheesi advertising permit number
- Printed and video property adverts must carry a Madmoun QR code, mandatory since 24 April 2023
- Brokerages and brokers must show their office (ORN) and broker (BRN) registration numbers in adverts
- Off-plan adverts must also show the developer, the project's escrow account number and the expected completion date

### Golden Visa through property

- Minimum value: property worth AED 2 million or more, in one property or several
- Term: ten years and renewable, according to the Dubai Land Department and GDRFA Dubai; the federal government portal shows a different term
- Jointly owned property counts only when the applicant's own share is worth AED 2 million or more
- The official DLD and GDRFA pages do not address off-plan property
- Below AED 2 million, DLD lists a two-year investor residence visa for a sole owner of property of any value, or a joint owner with a share of at least AED 400,000
- In April 2026 GDRFA Dubai and DLD agreed to move property residency services into GDRFA Dubai's system

### Owning and letting

- Service charges on jointly owned property need RERA's approval, which requires a budget approved by a certified audit firm (Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019, Article 27)
- A home may not be sold while its service charges are unpaid (Article 32)
- Every tenancy contract must be registered with RERA through Ejari; online registration costs AED 177.75
- Rent may rise at renewal only when it is more than 10% below the rent index average for similar homes, by 5%, 10%, 15% or at most 20% (Decree No. 43 of 2013)
- Changing tenancy terms or not renewing requires at least 90 days' notice before the contract ends, unless the contract says otherwise
- Ending a tenancy at expiry to sell, or for the owner or a first-degree relative to move in, requires at least 12 months' notice through a notary public or by registered mail

### Tax

- The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals
- A person's rental income from property held in their own name is not subject to corporate tax when the activity does not require a licence (Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023)
- Residential leases are generally exempt from VAT; the first supply of a new residential property within three years of completion is zero-rated

### Handover and defects

- Developers must repair or replace defective installations for one year from handover (Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019, Article 40)
- Developers must fix structural defects for ten years from the completion certificate (Article 40)
- Once a project has its completion certificate, the developer must register sold units in the names of buyers who have met their obligations (Law No. 13 of 2008, Article 8)
- If an off-plan buyer defaults, the developer may keep up to 40% of the unit's value on a project more than 60% complete, or up to 25% below that (Law No. 13 of 2008 as amended by Law No. 19 of 2020)

### Dubai in numbers

- In 2025 Dubai recorded more than 270,000 real estate transactions worth AED 917 billion, 20% more than in 2024 (Dubai Media Office, January 2026)
- Real estate transactions in the first quarter of 2026 reached AED 252 billion, up 31% on a year earlier (Dubai Land Department, April 2026)
- Dubai's population passed 4.58 million at the end of 2025, up 7.5% in a year (WAM, July 2026)

### Areas at a glance

| Area | Freehold | Public transport | Master developer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dubai Marina | Yes | Dubai Metro Red Line: Sobha Realty and DMCC stations. Dubai Tram: six stops, including Dubai Marina, Marina Towers, Dubai Marina Mall, JBR 1 and JBR 2 | Emaar |
| Downtown Dubai | Yes | Dubai Metro Red Line: Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall station | Emaar |
| Palm Jumeirah | Yes | Palm Monorail along the trunk, with stations including Gateway, Al Ittihad Park and Atlantis Aquaventure. Dubai Tram: the Palm Jumeirah stop, a walk from the Monorail's Gateway station | Nakheel |
| Dubai Hills Estate | Yes | No Metro station. RTA bus DH1 connects the community to Equiti station on the Red Line | Emaar and Meraas |
| Business Bay | Yes | Dubai Metro Red Line: Business Bay station | Dubai Properties (Dubai Holding) |
| Jumeirah Village Circle | Yes | No Metro station. Bus J01 runs to Mall of the Emirates, with other routes across the community | Nakheel |
| Dubai Creek Harbour | Yes | No Metro station yet. The Blue Line is due to open in September 2029 with a Dubai Creek Harbour station. Nearest station today: Creek, on the Green Line | Emaar |
| Dubai Islands | Yes | No Metro station. Nearest: Gold Souq on the Green Line, about ten minutes by road. RTA bus SM1 serves Souk Al Marfa at the entrance to the islands. Road access over the Infinity Bridge from Deira | Nakheel |
| Jumeirah Lake Towers | Yes | Dubai Metro Red Line: DMCC and Sobha Realty stations. Dubai Tram: the Jumeirah Lakes Towers stop, linked to DMCC station by footbridge. JLT Link electric shuttle: two loops connecting the clusters to the two Metro stations | DMCC |
| Mohammed Bin Rashid City | Yes | No Metro station. Nearest: Business Bay on the Red Line, a drive away. Most residents drive via Al Khail Road and Al Meydan Road | Meydan |
| Dubai South | Yes | Dubai Metro Red Line, Route 2020 branch: Expo 2020 station at Expo City Dubai, the end of the line. Al Maktoum International Airport is inside the district. Road access from Expo Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road | Dubai South |
| Arjan | Yes | No Metro station. RTA bus routes F36 and F37 serve the district. Nearest Red Line stations by car: Mall of the Emirates and Dubai Internet City | Dubai Properties (Dubai Holding) |

### Transport changes to know

- The Dubai Metro Blue Line is due to open on 9 September 2029, with a station at Dubai Creek Harbour
- Two Red Line stations near Dubai Marina were renamed: Sobha Realty (formerly Dubai Marina) and DMCC (formerly Jumeirah Lakes Towers)

## Dubai property glossary

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/dubai-property-glossary/

- **BRN (Broker Registration Number):** The registration number of an individual broker licensed by RERA. With the brokerage's ORN, it must appear in property adverts.
- **Completion certificate:** The certificate a planning authority issues when a building is complete: the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees or Dubai Municipality, depending on the area. It starts the developer's ten-year liability for structural defects.
- **DLD (Dubai Land Department):** The Dubai government department that registers property sales and leases and keeps the property register. Its regulatory arm is RERA.
- **Dubai REST:** The Dubai Land Department's real estate app: service charges, lease registration, rental and sales indices, off-plan project tracking, broker checks and the developer's e-NOC for a sale.
- **Ejari:** The system for registering tenancy contracts with RERA. Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 requires every lease to be registered.
- **Escrow account:** The bank account of a development project into which off-plan buyers' payments are made. Under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 the money may be used only to build that project.
- **Form A:** RERA's standard contract between a seller and the broker marketing the property.
- **Form B:** RERA's standard contract between a buyer and the broker acting for them.
- **Form F (MOU):** RERA's standard sale contract between buyer and seller, recording the price, the deposit and the transfer date. By custom the buyer pays a 10% deposit when it is signed.
- **Freehold:** Outright ownership with no time limit. Under Dubai Law No. 7 of 2006, non-UAE nationals can own freehold property in the areas designated for it.
- **Golden Visa:** A long-term UAE residence visa. Property investors in Dubai can apply with property worth AED 2 million or more.
- **Handover:** The delivery of a completed home to its buyer. It starts the developer's one-year liability for defective installations.
- **Leasehold (usufruct):** The right to use and benefit from property for a fixed term. Dubai Law No. 7 of 2006 allows non-UAE nationals to hold it for up to 99 years in designated areas.
- **Madmoun:** The QR code issued with each Trakheesi advertising permit, which lets anyone confirm a property advert is approved. It has been required on printed and video adverts since 24 April 2023.
- **Management entity:** The company that manages a jointly owned building or community and collects service charges under Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019. Owners are represented by an owners committee.
- **Mollak:** RERA's system for regulating jointly owned property: service charge budgets, owners' invoices and oversight of management companies.
- **NOC (No-objection certificate):** The developer's certificate that it does not object to a resale. For a sale in a freehold area DLD requires the electronic version, the e-NOC, issued through Dubai REST.
- **Off-plan:** A home bought from the developer before it is built, paid in stages under a payment plan.
- **Oqood:** The Dubai Land Department's interim register for off-plan homes, which records the buyer before a title deed exists. Registration costs 4% of the price plus AED 20.
- **ORN (Office Registration Number):** A brokerage's registration number with RERA. It must appear in the brokerage's property adverts.
- **Payment plan:** The schedule of payments for an off-plan home: a first payment on booking, instalments during construction and a balance at or after handover.
- **Registration trustee:** A DLD-approved centre that registers property sales. Its fee on a sale is AED 4,000 plus VAT, or AED 2,000 plus VAT under AED 500,000.
- **RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Agency):** The regulatory arm of the Dubai Land Department. It approves service charges, registers leases through Ejari and regulates brokers and property advertising.
- **Service Charge Index:** The Dubai Land Department's service for looking up the service charges RERA has approved for a jointly owned property, on the DLD website or in Dubai REST.
- **Service charges:** The annual charges owners pay to manage, operate, maintain and repair jointly owned property. RERA must approve them.
- **Smart Rental Index:** The Dubai Land Department's rent index since January 2025, which classifies buildings by specification, finishes, location and facilities. Rent increases at renewal depend on how far a rent sits below its average.
- **Snagging:** Inspecting a new home before accepting it and listing defects and incomplete work for the developer to fix. It is an industry practice, not a legal procedure.
- **SPA (Sale and purchase agreement):** The developer's sale contract for an off-plan home, setting out the price, the payment plan and the completion terms. Every off-plan sale must be entered in DLD's interim register.
- **Title deed:** The Dubai Land Department's certificate of ownership, issued when a sale is registered in the property register. Title deed fees on a sale total AED 520 for an apartment or villa.
- **Trakheesi:** The Dubai Land Department's system for issuing property advertising permits. Every property advert must show its Trakheesi permit number.

---

## Dubai Marina

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/dubai-marina/

Apartment towers on both sides of a man-made marina, with JBR beach, the tram and two Metro stations within reach.

Dubai Marina runs along a canal cut in from the sea and lined on both banks with residential towers. Marina Walk follows the water the whole way round, and Jumeirah Beach Residence sits between the towers and the sand.
If you are buying, almost everything on offer is an apartment. Studios and one-bedrooms fill the older towers near the Metro; larger homes and penthouses sit in the taller buildings with sea views. Ready homes dominate, so you can view what you buy.
If you are renting, the Marina is one of the easiest places in Dubai to live without a car. The tram loops through the district, the Red Line runs along its edge and most errands are on foot.
If you own here, your buyer pool is wide: end users who want the beach close, and investors who want a home that lets quickly. A clear view of the water or the sea is what sets one apartment apart from the next.

Homes: Studios and one- to four-bedroom apartments; Penthouses in the taller towers; Marina, sea and skyline views.
Suits: Buyers who want the beach and the water close; Professionals who commute by Metro or tram; Investors buying apartments to let.
Getting around: Dubai Metro Red Line: Sobha Realty and DMCC stations. Dubai Tram: six stops, including Dubai Marina, Marina Towers, Dubai Marina Mall, JBR 1 and JBR 2.
Master developer: Emaar.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Dubai Marina?**
Yes. Dubai Marina is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Dubai Marina?**
Studios and one- to four-bedroom apartments; penthouses in the taller towers; and Marina, sea and skyline views.

**How do you get around Dubai Marina by public transport?**
Dubai Metro Red Line: Sobha Realty and DMCC stations. Dubai Tram: six stops, including Dubai Marina, Marina Towers, Dubai Marina Mall, JBR 1 and JBR 2.

**Who is Dubai Marina a good fit for?**
Buyers who want the beach and the water close, professionals who commute by Metro or tram and investors buying apartments to let.

**Who is the master developer of Dubai Marina?**
Emaar.

**What are the landmarks in Dubai Marina?**
Marina Walk, Dubai Marina Mall, The Beach at JBR and Ain Dubai on Bluewaters.

**Who rents in Dubai Marina?**
Tenants here are mostly single professionals and couples who want the beach, the tram and the Metro without owning a car.

**What should I know before selling a home in Dubai Marina?**
A marina or sea view and a tower with a well-run owners' association are what buyers ask about first, so have the service charge history ready.

**Which areas are next to Dubai Marina?**
Jumeirah Lake Towers and Palm Jumeirah.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Dubai Marina?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works it out for any price.

---

## Downtown Dubai

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/downtown-dubai/

The district around Burj Khalifa and The Dubai Mall, where the Boulevard links the towers, the fountain and the opera house.

Downtown Dubai is the block of the city around Burj Khalifa, The Dubai Mall and the Dubai Fountain. Mohammed Bin Rashid Boulevard loops through it, and Dubai Opera sits at one end.
Buyers choose between compact one-bedrooms in the Boulevard buildings and large residences in the towers that face the fountain or Burj Khalifa itself. Everything is an apartment, and most buildings are complete and lived in.
For tenants, Downtown is the place to be if you work in DIFC or Business Bay and want to walk to the mall, the Metro and the restaurants on the Boulevard. Check the parking and the service charge before you sign.
For owners, the address itself does much of the selling. A fountain view or a direct line of sight to the tower is what separates a quick sale from a slow one, so lead with the view in your listing.

Homes: One- to four-bedroom apartments; Penthouses and large residences; Burj Khalifa, fountain and boulevard views.
Suits: Buyers who want the city on foot; Owners who value a landmark view; Investors letting to professionals.
Getting around: Dubai Metro Red Line: Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall station.
Master developer: Emaar.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Downtown Dubai?**
Yes. Downtown Dubai is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Downtown Dubai?**
One- to four-bedroom apartments; penthouses and large residences; and Burj Khalifa, fountain and boulevard views.

**How do you get around Downtown Dubai by public transport?**
Dubai Metro Red Line: Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall station.

**Who is Downtown Dubai a good fit for?**
Buyers who want the city on foot, owners who value a landmark view and investors letting to professionals.

**Who is the master developer of Downtown Dubai?**
Emaar.

**What are the landmarks in Downtown Dubai?**
Burj Khalifa, The Dubai Mall, Dubai Fountain, Dubai Opera, Mohammed Bin Rashid Boulevard and Burj Park.

**Who rents in Downtown Dubai?**
Renters are professionals from DIFC and Business Bay, and short-stay guests in the buildings that allow holiday lets.

**What should I know before selling a home in Downtown Dubai?**
Buyers compare your apartment with the others in the same tower, so a renovated kitchen or a rare view is what justifies a higher ask.

**Which areas are next to Downtown Dubai?**
Business Bay and Mohammed Bin Rashid City.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Downtown Dubai?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works it out for any price.

---

## Palm Jumeirah

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/palm-jumeirah/

The palm-shaped island: villas along the fronds, apartment buildings and hotels on the trunk, resorts on the crescent.

Palm Jumeirah is a man-made island laid out as a palm. The trunk carries apartment buildings and hotels, the fronds carry villas, and the crescent that wraps the outside is given over to resorts, with Atlantis at its centre.
If you are buying a villa, most of them on the fronds open straight onto their own beach. Apartment buyers on the trunk and the crescent get sea views or a view back across the water to the Marina towers. Penthouses and branded residences sit in the newer buildings.
Tenants here pay for the beach and the privacy. Families take the frond villas; couples take trunk apartments near Nakheel Mall and the Monorail. A car is still useful, because the island has one road in.
If you are selling, Palm Jumeirah is one of the few areas in Dubai where a beachfront villa is a category of its own. Buyers want to know the plot, the beach frontage and whether the home has been extended, so have the drawings ready.

Homes: Beachfront villas on the fronds; Apartments and penthouses on the trunk and crescent; Sea, beach and skyline views.
Suits: Families who want a villa on the beach; Buyers looking for a landmark address; Owners who want a home by the sea in the city.
Getting around: Palm Monorail along the trunk, with stations including Gateway, Al Ittihad Park and Atlantis Aquaventure. Dubai Tram: the Palm Jumeirah stop, a walk from the Monorail's Gateway station.
Master developer: Nakheel.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Palm Jumeirah?**
Yes. Palm Jumeirah is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Palm Jumeirah?**
Beachfront villas on the fronds; apartments and penthouses on the trunk and crescent; and sea, beach and skyline views.

**How do you get around Palm Jumeirah by public transport?**
Palm Monorail along the trunk, with stations including Gateway, Al Ittihad Park and Atlantis Aquaventure. Dubai Tram: the Palm Jumeirah stop, a walk from the Monorail's Gateway station.

**Who is Palm Jumeirah a good fit for?**
Families who want a villa on the beach, buyers looking for a landmark address and owners who want a home by the sea in the city.

**Who is the master developer of Palm Jumeirah?**
Nakheel.

**What are the landmarks in Palm Jumeirah?**
Atlantis The Palm, Nakheel Mall, Palm West Beach, Al Ittihad Park and The View at The Palm.

**Who rents in Palm Jumeirah?**
Families rent the frond villas for the private beach, and couples rent trunk apartments to be near the mall, the restaurants and the Monorail.

**What should I know before selling a home in Palm Jumeirah?**
Villa buyers here pay for beach frontage and plot size above everything else, so lead with both and keep any extension approvals to hand.

**Which areas are next to Palm Jumeirah?**
Dubai Marina.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Palm Jumeirah?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works it out for any price.

## Dubai Hills Estate

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/dubai-hills-estate/

A planned community built around a golf course, a central park and Dubai Hills Mall.

Dubai Hills Estate is a planned community with a golf course at its centre, a long central park and Dubai Hills Mall on its northern edge. It is part of the wider Mohammed Bin Rashid City plan but is marketed and run as its own address.
Buyers get a real choice of home type. Villas and townhouses sit on quiet streets with gardens, many backing onto the course or the park. Apartment buildings cluster near the mall and along the park, which is where first-time buyers tend to look.
For tenants, this is a family area. The schools, the park and the mall are inside the community, and King's College Hospital is on its edge. There is no Metro, so budget for a car or the bus to Equiti station.
For owners, demand comes from families moving up from apartments and from buyers who want green space without leaving the city. A garden that faces the course or the park is the detail that moves a villa fastest.

Homes: Villas and townhouses, many with gardens; Apartments near the park and mall; Golf course and park views.
Suits: Families who want a villa and a garden; Buyers who want green space in the city; Owners who drive to work.
Getting around: No Metro station. RTA bus DH1 connects the community to Equiti station on the Red Line.
Master developer: Emaar and Meraas.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Dubai Hills Estate?**
Yes. Dubai Hills Estate is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Dubai Hills Estate?**
Villas and townhouses, many with gardens; apartments near the park and mall; and golf course and park views.

**How do you get around Dubai Hills Estate by public transport?**
No Metro station. RTA bus DH1 connects the community to Equiti station on the Red Line.

**Who is Dubai Hills Estate a good fit for?**
Families who want a villa and a garden, buyers who want green space in the city and owners who drive to work.

**Who is the master developer of Dubai Hills Estate?**
Emaar and Meraas.

**What are the landmarks in Dubai Hills Estate?**
Dubai Hills Mall, Dubai Hills Golf Club, Dubai Hills Park and King's College Hospital London Dubai.

**Who rents in Dubai Hills Estate?**
Families with school-age children rent the villas and townhouses, and young professionals rent the apartments by the park and the mall.

**What should I know before selling a home in Dubai Hills Estate?**
Villa buyers here compare plots, garden orientation and whether the home backs onto the course or the park, so state all three in your listing.

**Which areas are next to Dubai Hills Estate?**
Mohammed Bin Rashid City and arjan.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Dubai Hills Estate?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works it out for any price.

## Business Bay

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/business-bay/

A mixed district of offices, hotels and apartment towers along the Dubai Water Canal, next door to Downtown Dubai.

Business Bay lies south of Downtown Dubai along the Dubai Water Canal. Offices, hotels and residential towers share the same streets, and a promenade runs along both banks of the canal.
Buyers here get Downtown's location at a different price point. Homes are apartments, from studios to three-bedrooms, in towers that face the canal, the Burj Khalifa skyline or each other. Ready buildings and new off-plan towers sit side by side.
Tenants are mostly people who work in the district or in DIFC and Downtown and want a short commute. Business Bay Metro station is on the Red Line, and the canal walk links the district to Downtown and Jumeirah on foot.
If you are selling, the canal view is the premium. The towers vary a lot in build quality and management, so buyers will ask about the service charge and the owners' association before they ask about the finish.

Homes: Studios and one- to three-bedroom apartments; Canal and skyline views; Ready homes and new off-plan towers.
Suits: Professionals who work in the centre; Buyers who want to be close to Downtown; Investors buying apartments to let.
Getting around: Dubai Metro Red Line: Business Bay station.
Master developer: Dubai Properties (Dubai Holding).
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Business Bay?**
Yes. Business Bay is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Business Bay?**
Studios and one- to three-bedroom apartments, canal and skyline views and ready homes and new off-plan towers.

**How do you get around Business Bay by public transport?**
Dubai Metro Red Line: Business Bay station.

**Who is Business Bay a good fit for?**
Professionals who work in the centre, buyers who want to be close to Downtown and investors buying apartments to let.

**Who is the master developer of Business Bay?**
Dubai Properties (Dubai Holding).

**What are the landmarks in Business Bay?**
Dubai Water Canal, Marasi Promenade, Bay Avenue and Bay Square.

**Who rents in Business Bay?**
Tenants are office workers from Business Bay, DIFC and Downtown who want to walk or take one Metro stop to work.

**What should I know before selling a home in Business Bay?**
The canal-facing towers sell on the view and the rest sell on price, so know which side of that line your apartment sits.

**Which areas are next to Business Bay?**
Downtown Dubai and Mohammed Bin Rashid City.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Business Bay?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works it out for any price.

## Jumeirah Village Circle

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/jumeirah-village-circle/

A circular community of low- and mid-rise buildings, townhouses and villas, with parks at its centre and new buildings going up around them.

Jumeirah Village Circle, or JVC, is laid out as a ring with parks in the middle. Low- and mid-rise apartment buildings line the outer roads, and townhouses and villas sit on the quieter streets inside.
Buyers come here because the entry point sits below the waterfront districts. Much of the stock is new: studios and one- and two-bedrooms in buildings sold off-plan, alongside ready homes you can move into now. Circle Mall sits in the middle of the community.
For tenants, JVC is one of the better-value addresses between the Marina and Dubai Hills. There is no Metro, so most residents drive; bus J01 runs to Mall of the Emirates for the Red Line.
For owners, the buyer pool is investors looking for a rental home and first-time buyers trading up from renting. The buildings differ widely, so a well-run building with a pool and a gym and a park view is what separates your apartment from the rest.

Homes: Studios and one- to three-bedroom apartments; Townhouses and villas; Ready homes and off-plan buildings.
Suits: First-time buyers; Investors looking for rental homes; Buyers who want space for their budget.
Getting around: No Metro station. Bus J01 runs to Mall of the Emirates, with other routes across the community.
Master developer: Nakheel.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

**Can foreigners buy property in Jumeirah Village Circle?**
Yes. Jumeirah Village Circle is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Jumeirah Village Circle?**
Studios and one- to three-bedroom apartments, townhouses and villas and ready homes and off-plan buildings.

**How do you get around Jumeirah Village Circle by public transport?**
No Metro station. Bus J01 runs to Mall of the Emirates, with other routes across the community.

**Who is Jumeirah Village Circle a good fit for?**
First-time buyers, investors looking for rental homes and buyers who want space for their budget.

**Who is the master developer of Jumeirah Village Circle?**
Nakheel.

**What are the landmarks in Jumeirah Village Circle?**
Circle Mall, the JVC community parks and Floareá Skies by Mashriq Elite.

**Who rents in Jumeirah Village Circle?**
Renters are young professionals and small families who want a new building and a lower rent than the coast, and who drive to work.

**What should I know before selling a home in Jumeirah Village Circle?**
Buyers weigh your building against dozens of newer ones nearby, so a strong management record and a park or pool view matter more than the finish.

**Which areas are next to Jumeirah Village Circle?**
Arjan.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Jumeirah Village Circle?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. ## Dubai Creek Harbour

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/dubai-creek-harbour/

A waterfront district on Dubai Creek beside the Ras Al Khor sanctuary, with the Downtown skyline across the water and a Blue Line station on the way.

Dubai Creek Harbour sits on the creek beside the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary. From the promenade, you look straight across the water to Burj Khalifa and the Downtown skyline.
Buyers here choose between apartment buildings that are already lived in around Creek Marina and off-plan towers sold on payment plans. Homes run from one to four bedrooms, and the view is either the creek, the skyline or the sanctuary.
For tenants, the district is quieter than Downtown and the promenade, Creek Beach and the marina are on your doorstep. The nearest Metro today is Creek on the Green Line; the Blue Line will add a station inside the district when it opens in September 2029.
For owners, the Blue Line is the thing to watch. A station on the doorstep changes who will buy, so an apartment close to the station site will draw more interest than one at the far end of the promenade.

Homes: One- to four-bedroom apartments; Off-plan homes on payment plans; Creek, skyline and sanctuary views.
Suits: Buyers who want a new home on the water; Off-plan buyers planning around a payment plan; Buyers who want a view of the skyline.
Getting around: No Metro station yet. The Blue Line is due to open in September 2029 with a Dubai Creek Harbour station. Nearest station today: Creek, on the Green Line.
Master developer: Emaar.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Dubai Creek Harbour?**
Yes. Dubai Creek Harbour is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Dubai Creek Harbour?**
One- to four-bedroom apartments; off-plan homes on payment plans; and Creek, skyline and sanctuary views.

**How do you get around Dubai Creek Harbour by public transport?**
No Metro station yet. The Blue Line is due to open in September 2029 with a Dubai Creek Harbour station. Nearest station today: Creek, on the Green Line.

**Who is Dubai Creek Harbour a good fit for?**
Buyers who want a new home on the water, off-plan buyers planning around a payment plan and buyers who want a view of the skyline.

**Who is the master developer of Dubai Creek Harbour?**
Emaar.

**What are the landmarks in Dubai Creek Harbour?**
Creek Marina, Creek Beach, the Dubai Creek Harbour promenade and Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary.

**Who rents in Dubai Creek Harbour?**
Tenants are couples and small families who want a new apartment on the water and are happy to drive until the Blue Line opens.

**What should I know before selling a home in Dubai Creek Harbour?**
Buyers of resale here compare your apartment with the developer's off-plan releases next door, so a ready home with a skyline view is your strongest card.

**Which areas are next to Dubai Creek Harbour?**
Downtown Dubai and Mohammed Bin Rashid City.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Dubai Creek Harbour?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. ## Dubai Islands

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/dubai-islands/

Nakheel's five islands off the Deira coast, reached by the Infinity Bridge, with beachfront apartments and villas going up around long public beaches.

Dubai Islands is a group of five man-made islands off the coast of Deira, developed by Nakheel. The islands are named Central, Marina, Shore, Golf and Elite, and they are linked to the city by the Infinity Bridge and to each other by smaller bridges.
If you are buying, most of what is on offer is off-plan: beachfront apartment buildings, branded residences and villa communities such as Bay Villas. Nakheel sells the land and builds the beaches and roads; the homes come from a growing list of developers, including Mashriq Elite's Floareá Breeze. Check each project's escrow account and construction progress before you commit.
If you plan to rent here, the islands are still being built, so ready homes are few and the shops and restaurants are mostly at Souk Al Marfa for now. The nearest Metro is Gold Souq on the Green Line, a short drive over the bridge, and there is no station on the islands.
If you own a plot or an off-plan home here, your buyer is someone who wants a beach address that is not Palm Jumeirah. A direct beach view and a short walk to the sand are what buyers pay for, so show both.

Homes: Beachfront apartments and penthouses; Villas and townhouses in gated communities; Off-plan homes on payment plans.
Suits: Buyers who want a new beach address; Off-plan buyers planning around a payment plan; Buyers who like Deira and the old city close by.
Getting around: No Metro station. Nearest: Gold Souq on the Green Line, about ten minutes by road. RTA bus SM1 serves Souk Al Marfa at the entrance to the islands. Road access over the Infinity Bridge from Deira.
Master developer: Nakheel.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Dubai Islands?**
Yes. Dubai Islands is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Dubai Islands?**
Beachfront apartments and penthouses, villas and townhouses in gated communities and off-plan homes on payment plans.

**How do you get around Dubai Islands by public transport?**
No Metro station. Nearest: Gold Souq on the Green Line, about ten minutes by road. RTA bus SM1 serves Souk Al Marfa at the entrance to the islands. Road access over the Infinity Bridge from Deira.

**Who is Dubai Islands a good fit for?**
Buyers who want a new beach address, off-plan buyers planning around a payment plan and buyers who like Deira and the old city close by.

**Who is the master developer of Dubai Islands?**
Nakheel.

**What are the landmarks in Dubai Islands?**
Infinity Bridge, Souk Al Marfa, the Blue Flag beach, Rixos Dubai Islands, Bay Villas and Floareá Breeze by Mashriq Elite.

**Who rents in Dubai Islands?**
The first tenants are couples and small families who want a beach apartment and do not mind that the islands are still being built around them.

**What should I know before selling a home in Dubai Islands?**
Most resale here is off-plan, so your buyer will compare your payment plan and construction progress with the developer's own releases.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Dubai Islands?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. ## Jumeirah Lake Towers

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/jumeirah-lake-towers/

A freehold district of towers in 26 clusters around three lakes and a park, with two Red Line stations and the Marina across Sheikh Zayed Road.

Jumeirah Lake Towers, or JLT, sits on the inland side of Sheikh Zayed Road opposite Dubai Marina. Its towers stand in 26 clusters lettered A to Z around three lakes and a central park, and the DMCC free zone has its headquarters in Almas Tower at the centre.
Buyers get apartments from studios to four-bedrooms, with penthouses in a few of the taller towers. Almost everything is ready, since the district was built out in the 2000s and early 2010s, and the towers vary in age, finish and management. Uptown Dubai, DMCC's newer district on the southern edge, adds a taller skyline.
For tenants, JLT is one of the best-connected areas in the city. DMCC and Sobha Realty stations are both on the Red Line, the Jumeirah Lakes Towers tram stop links to DMCC station by footbridge, and the JLT Link electric shuttle runs two loops around the clusters. Many of the companies in the free zone are within walking distance of home.
If you are selling, your apartment is one of many in a district with a lot of stock, so the tower matters as much as the unit. A lake view, a well-kept building and a short walk to a station are what move a sale here.

Homes: Studios and one- to four-bedroom apartments; Penthouses in a few of the taller towers; Lake, park and Marina skyline views.
Suits: Professionals who work in DMCC or the Marina; Buyers who want the Marina's location at a different price point; Investors buying apartments to let.
Getting around: Dubai Metro Red Line: DMCC and Sobha Realty stations. Dubai Tram: the Jumeirah Lakes Towers stop, linked to DMCC station by footbridge. JLT Link electric shuttle: two loops connecting the clusters to the two Metro stations.
Master developer: DMCC.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
Yes. Jumeirah Lake Towers is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
Studios and one- to four-bedroom apartments; penthouses in a few of the taller towers; and Lake, park and Marina skyline views.

**How do you get around Jumeirah Lake Towers by public transport?**
Dubai Metro Red Line: DMCC and Sobha Realty stations. Dubai Tram: the Jumeirah Lakes Towers stop, linked to DMCC station by footbridge. JLT Link electric shuttle: two loops connecting the clusters to the two Metro stations.

**Who is Jumeirah Lake Towers a good fit for?**
Professionals who work in DMCC or the Marina, buyers who want the Marina's location at a different price point and investors buying apartments to let.

**Who is the master developer of Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
DMCC.

**What are the landmarks in Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
Almas Tower, JLT Park, Lake Almas West, Lake Almas East, JLT Lake and Uptown Dubai.

**Which schools and nurseries are near Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
Dewdrops Nursery; Learning Ladders Nursery; Paddington Nursery; Oakfield Early Learning Centre; and Emirates International School (The Meadows, nearby).

**Who rents in Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
Tenants are free-zone employees and Marina workers who want a Metro station close and a lower rent than the towers across the road.

**What should I know before selling a home in Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
Buyers here shop by cluster and tower before they shop by apartment, so a strong building record and a lake view are what you lead with.

**Which areas are next to Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
Dubai Marina.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Jumeirah Lake Towers?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. ## Mohammed Bin Rashid City

URL: https://expertcarerealestate.com/areas/mohammed-bin-rashid-city/

A large master plan south of Downtown Dubai, home to District One and its Crystal Lagoon, Sobha Hartland, Sobha Hartland II and the Meydan racecourse.

Mohammed Bin Rashid City, or MBR City, is a master plan by Meydan that stretches from Business Bay and Downtown Dubai towards the Ras Al Khor sanctuary and Al Khail Road. Inside it sit several communities with their own names: District One around the Crystal Lagoon, Sobha Hartland on the creek side, Sobha Hartland II next to it, Meydan Horizon and District 11.
Buyers have the widest range of home types of any area near the centre. District One is villas and mansions on the lagoon with some apartment phases. Sobha Hartland and Hartland II mix villas, townhouses and towers; Hartland II is sold off-plan around its own lagoon.
For tenants, MBR City is a car area. There is no Metro station; Business Bay on the Red Line is the nearest, and most residents drive via Al Khail Road or Al Meydan Road. In return you get lagoons, parks and two international schools inside Sobha Hartland.
If you are selling, your buyer is a family who wants a villa or a large apartment close to Downtown without the density. Off-plan supply in Hartland II and District One West competes with resale, so a ready home with a lagoon or skyline view is what stands out.

Homes: Villas and mansions around the lagoons; Townhouses in Sobha Hartland and Hartland II; Apartments in mid-rise buildings and new towers.
Suits: Families who want a villa near Downtown; Buyers who want a lagoon or park on the doorstep; Off-plan buyers planning around a payment plan.
Getting around: No Metro station. Nearest: Business Bay on the Red Line, a drive away. Most residents drive via Al Khail Road and Al Meydan Road.
Master developer: Meydan.
Ownership: freehold, open to buyers of any nationality.

### Questions

**Can foreigners buy property in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
Yes. Mohammed Bin Rashid City is a freehold area, so buyers of any nationality can own homes there outright, and they do not need to live in the UAE to buy.

**What types of property are there in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
Villas and mansions around the lagoons, townhouses in Sobha Hartland and Hartland II and apartments in mid-rise buildings and new towers.

**How do you get around Mohammed Bin Rashid City by public transport?**
No Metro station. Nearest: Business Bay on the Red Line, a drive away. Most residents drive via Al Khail Road and Al Meydan Road.

**Who is Mohammed Bin Rashid City a good fit for?**
Families who want a villa near Downtown, buyers who want a lagoon or park on the doorstep and off-plan buyers planning around a payment plan.

**Who is the master developer of Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
Meydan.

**What are the landmarks in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
District One Crystal Lagoon, Meydan Racecourse, Meydan One Mall (under construction), Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary and Sobha Hartland II lagoon.

**Which schools and nurseries are near Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai.

**Who rents in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
Families with children at the two schools in Sobha Hartland rent the villas and townhouses, and professionals from Business Bay rent the apartments.

**What should I know before selling a home in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
Resale here competes with the developers' own off-plan launches next door, so a ready home with a lagoon or skyline view is your advantage.

**Which areas are next to Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
Downtown Dubai, business Bay, Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai Creek Harbour.

**What are the costs of buying a home in Mohammed Bin Rashid City?**
The same fees apply across Dubai. A ready home carries the 4% DLD transfer fee, AED 520 in title deed fees, the registration trustee fee and usually a 2% agency fee plus VAT; an off-plan home carries 4% Oqood registration plus AED 20. The [buying costs calculator](https://expertcarerealestate.com/buying-costs/) works it out for any price.
